title: By the angels standing in perfect rows.
subtitle: Why ranks of angels are sworn by

row.title: a line is just a line
a row is worship
sub: like the angels before their Lord

then: Ibn Masud and many others said these are {idea}the angels{/idea}. Qatadah said they form ranks in the heavens. The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to form rows {idea}as the angels do before their Lord{/idea}: complete the front rows and stand close.
now: You arrive at the mosque and stand at the back with gaps on either side, half thinking about your phone. {idea}The angels are standing in rows too, right now, in the heavens.{/idea} Your row on earth echoes theirs.
old: Where I stand in prayer does not really matter.
new: When I straighten my row, I am standing the way the angels stand.
try: In your next congregational prayer, fill the gap beside you and straighten your line.

title: By the angels who drive the clouds.
subtitle: The unseen workers behind the weather
then: Ibn Masud said these too are {idea}the angels{/idea}. As-Suddi and others said they {idea}drive the clouds.{/idea} For people living in the dry valleys of Makkah, clouds meant rain and life.
now: You check the weather app and grumble at rain on your day off. {idea}Behind every cloud is a command being carried out{/idea}, and the rain is somebody's crop, somebody's drinking water.
old: The weather is just something that happens.
new: Even the clouds are moved by Allah's servants, on His orders.
try: When you see clouds or rain today, say a short thanks for the rain and its blessing.

title: By the angels who bring the reminder.
subtitle: The message came through a chain of trust
then: As-Suddi said {idea}the angels bring the Scriptures and the Quran from Allah to mankind.{/idea} Three oaths by the angels come before the main statement, like a solemn opening before something important is said.
now: The Quran app on your phone sits between a game and a shopping app. It looks like just another app. {idea}The words in it travelled from Allah, through angels, to you.{/idea}
old: The Quran is a book I can open whenever.
new: The Quran is a message brought down by angels, and it reached me.
try: Before you next open the Quran, pause for a second and remember where it came from.

title: Your God is One.
subtitle: What the three oaths were leading to
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the statement the oaths confirm: {idea}there is no god worthy of worship but He.{/idea} The Quraysh worshipped many idols and mocked the Prophet ﷺ for calling to one God.
now: Your boss wants one thing, your parents another, your friends a third, and your feed tells you who to be. {trap}You are pulled in ten directions.{/trap} {idea}One God means one direction.{/idea}
old: I have to keep everyone happy.
new: I only have One to answer to, and that makes life simpler.
try: When you feel torn today, ask: what would please Allah here? Let that decide.

title: Lord of every sunrise.
subtitle: The One God runs the whole sky
then: Ibn Kathir says He is the Sovereign who controls {idea}the stars and planets that rise in the east and set in the west.{/idea} The sun rises from a different point through the year, and He is Lord of each one.
now: Your alarm goes off before dawn. Outside, the sun is coming up from a slightly different spot than last month. {idea}Every single sunrise is under His care{/idea}, including the one that started your day.
old: Sunrise is just the start of another busy day.
new: Each sunrise is placed there by my Lord, and so is my day.
try: Watch the sunrise or the morning light once this week, and say the morning remembrance.

title: The stars are decoration for the nearest sky.
subtitle: Beauty placed for those who look up
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah adorned the lowest heaven {reward}for those on earth who look at it{/reward}, and the stars give them light. He links it to 67:5 and 15:16, where the sky is beautified for the beholders.
now: You have not looked at the night sky properly in months. Streetlights, screens, ceilings. {reward}The decoration is still up there{/reward}, put there for you to see.
old: The sky is just there; I hardly notice it.
new: The stars are a gift of beauty, and I am one of the people they were placed for.
try: Turn off a light tonight and look at the sky for a few minutes.

title: The sky is also guarded against rebel devils.
subtitle: Beauty and protection in the same thing
then: Ibn Kathir says this guards the heaven {idea}as it should be protected{/idea} from every insolent devil. When one tries to eavesdrop on the news in the heavens, {trap}a piercing fire comes and burns him.{/trap}
now: You install security on your phone and lock the front door at night. You protect what matters. {idea}Allah protected His revelation far more carefully{/idea}, so what reached you is clean.
old: Who knows what got mixed into the message over time.
new: Allah guarded His revelation from the start, so I can trust it.
try: Say a'udhu billah before reciting today, asking Allah to guard your heart as He guarded His word.

title: They cannot listen in. They are struck from every side.
subtitle: No way in to the exalted assembly
then: Ibn Kathir says the devils {trap}cannot reach the higher group{/trap}, the angels in the heavens, when they speak of Allah's laws and decrees. They are hit from all directions they try to approach from.
now: A horoscope pops up in your feed. A relative swears by a fortune teller. {idea}The unseen is locked away from them{/idea}, struck from every side. Nobody has a back door into what Allah decrees.
old: Maybe some people really can see what is coming for me.
new: The unseen belongs to Allah, and those who claim it are cut off.
try: Next time a horoscope or prediction shows up, scroll past and say tawakkaltu ala Allah.

title: Driven back, and a lasting punishment ahead.
subtitle: Rebellion gets pushed away
then: Ibn Kathir says the devils are {trap}rejected, repelled and prevented{/trap} from reaching the heaven. In the Hereafter they will have an ongoing punishment, as 67:5 also says.
now: You keep pushing at something you know is wrong: the shortcut at work, the habit you hide. It never quite gets you where you want. {idea}Some doors are shut for a reason.{/idea} Turning back is always open.
old: If I push hard enough, I can get away with it.
new: Going against Allah's order only pushes me further away, so I would rather turn back.
try: Name one thing you keep forcing that you know is not right. Stop pushing at it today.

title: One word snatched, nine lies added.
subtitle: Why stolen whispers are not to be trusted
then: Ibn Abbas said devils once sat listening, then {trap}added nine words of their own{/trap} to every word they heard. When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, {idea}the flaming fire would strike them every time.{/idea}
now: A rumour in the family group has one true detail, so everyone believes the rest. A scam email uses your real name. {trap}One true piece makes the lies feel safe.{/trap}
old: If part of it is true, the rest is probably true too.
new: A little truth is often used to carry a lot of falsehood.
try: Before you forward the next message today, check whether all of it is true.

title: Ask them: are you harder to make, or the heavens?
subtitle: Made of sticky clay, doubting a return

row.title: I am too much to remake

then: Ibn Masud said they {idea}admitted the heavens were harder to create{/idea} than they were. So why deny the resurrection? Mujahid and others said sticky clay is {idea}mud that clings to itself{/idea}, a humble start.
now: Clay stuck to your shoes after a rainy walk, hard to scrape off. That is the material you began from. {idea}The One who built the sky out of nothing is not stretched by you.{/idea}
old: I am too complicated a case for anything to fix.
new: I began as clay, and the One who made the heavens can easily remake me.
try: Touch some soil or clay today and remember where you came from.

title: You were amazed, and they were laughing.
subtitle: Two reactions to the same truth

row.title: they laugh, so it is silly
the laughing is the strange part

then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was {idea}astounded{/idea} that they denied the resurrection while he was certain of it. Qatadah said he was amazed by {trap}the mockery of the misguided.{/trap}
now: You mention you are fasting or going to pray, and a colleague smirks. You feel small for a moment. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ was laughed at too, over the very same truth.{/idea}
old: If people laugh at my faith, maybe I look foolish.
new: Being mocked for the truth puts me in good company.
try: If someone teases you about your faith today, answer with a calm smile and carry on.

title: Reminded, and still not remembering.
subtitle: When reminders bounce off

row.title: no attention
sub: they do not take it in

then: Ibn Kathir describes them as paying {trap}no attention{/trap} when reminded. They heard the warnings in Makkah again and again. {trap}The words reached their ears and stopped there.{/trap}
now: You have heard the same Friday talk about backbiting many times. You nod, then go back to the group chat. {idea}A reminder only works if you let it in.{/idea}
old: I already know this, so I can tune out.
new: Knowing is not the same as remembering; I need to let it change something.
try: Take one reminder you have heard many times and act on it once today.

title: They see a sign and make it a joke.
subtitle: Mockery as a way to avoid thinking
then: Ibn Kathir says an ayah here means {idea}clear evidence and proof{/idea}. Mujahid and Qatadah said {trap}they make fun of it.{/trap} Laughter was easier than facing what the sign meant.
now: Someone shares a serious point in the chat and you reply with a laughing emoji, because thinking about it is uncomfortable. {trap}A joke can be a door you shut on purpose.{/trap}
old: Laughing it off keeps things light.
new: Sometimes my joke is a way of not facing a sign Allah sent me.
try: The next time you feel like joking away something serious, stop and think about it for one minute first.

title: They called it plain magic.
subtitle: Labelling the truth to avoid it
then: They said, in Ibn Kathir's words, {trap}this you have brought is nothing but plain magic.{/trap} Calling it magic let them ignore what it said without having to answer it.
now: You hear advice you do not like and call it extreme, or old-fashioned, or preachy. {trap}The label saves you from thinking.{/trap} {idea}The question is whether it is true.{/idea}
old: Once I name something as nonsense, I do not have to think about it.
new: A label is not a reply; I owe the truth a real look.
try: Think of one reminder you dismissed with a label. Look at what it actually said.

title: Dust and bones, raised again? They could not believe it.
subtitle: The doubt that dust can live

row.title: Who is doing it
sub: the One who made the heavens

then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}thought it unlikely and did not believe it.{/trap} Just before this, Allah reminded them that the heavens are harder to create than they are. Their doubt looked at the dust, not at the Creator.
now: You stand at a burial and watch the soil go in. It feels so final. {idea}The question is not how little is left, but how great is the One who raises.{/idea}
old: Once a body is dust, there is nothing left to bring back.
new: The resurrection depends on Allah's power, not on what remains of me.
try: Make dua today for someone you have lost, trusting you will meet again.

title: And our forefathers too? Yes, them too.
subtitle: The oldest generations are not forgotten
then: The deniers added a second question: {trap}and also our fathers of old?{/trap} Ibn Kathir treats it with the previous verse: they thought it unlikely. {idea}The answer in the next verse covers them all.{/idea}
now: You look at an old family photo: great-grandparents whose names nobody remembers. {idea}They will stand up on that Day too{/idea}, and so will you, and your grandchildren.
old: The people of long ago are simply gone.
new: Every generation, however old, will be raised and meet its Lord.
try: Make dua today for your grandparents and those before them by name, if you know them.

title: Say: Yes, and you will be humbled.
subtitle: A short answer to a long doubt
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to answer: {idea}yes, you will be raised{/idea} after becoming dust and bones, and {trap}put to shame before His great might.{/trap} He links it to 27:87: all shall come to Him humbled.
now: Someone at work talks big, never admits a mistake, laughs at religion. You might be that person sometimes. {idea}Everyone comes to Him humble in the end.{/idea} Choosing humility now is easier.
old: Admitting I am small makes me weak.
new: Humbling myself before Allah now is better than being humbled later.
try: Admit one small mistake to someone today, plainly, without excuses.

title: One shout, and they are standing, staring.
subtitle: No time between the call and the gathering
then: Ibn Kathir says it will be {idea}a single command from Allah{/idea}: He calls them once to come out of the earth, and they stand before Him, {trap}staring at the horrors of the Day.{/trap}
now: A phone call at 3am. One sentence, and your whole life changes. You know that feeling. {idea}The Day will come like that: one call, no build-up.{/idea} So the getting ready happens now.
old: I will have time to prepare when the end gets closer.
new: It comes with a single call, so today is my time to prepare.
try: Do one thing today you would want done if you knew the call was close.

title: Woe to us, this is the Day of Recompense.
subtitle: Regret that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir says they will {trap}blame themselves and admit they wronged themselves{/trap}, filled with regret when regret no longer helps. They see with their own eyes what they had mocked.
now: You snapped at your mother and she went quiet. That night you feel the sting. {reward}That sting, today, is a gift.{/reward} Regret while there is time can still become an apology, a change, a tawbah.
old: Regret is just a bad feeling to push away.
new: Regret now is a mercy, because now it can still turn into repentance.
try: Turn one regret into action today: an apology, a repayment, or a sincere istighfar.

title: This is the Day of Sorting you used to deny.
subtitle: The day everything is separated out

row.title: you denied it
sub: used to call it a lie

then: Ibn Kathir says the angels and believers will say this {trap}as a rebuke{/trap}. Then Allah will command the angels to {idea}separate the disbelievers from the believers{/idea} where they stand.
now: In life things blur: who was right in the argument, whose money it really was, whether that comment was a joke. {idea}That Day, everything gets sorted cleanly.{/idea} Live as if the sorting is honest, because it will be.
old: Things are so blurry that no one will ever know who was really right.
new: Allah will sort everything clearly, so I can be honest now.
try: Settle one blurry matter today: return something, or tell the truth about something.

title: Gather the wrongdoers with their kind.
subtitle: You end up with the people like you
then: Umar and others said azwaj means {idea}those who are like them{/idea}: people of the same sin gathered together. Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}their friends.{/idea} Their idols are gathered with them too.
now: Look at the five people you spend the most time with, online and off. What do you talk about? What do you laugh at? {idea}You are slowly becoming their kind, and they yours.{/idea}
old: Who I hang out with does not say anything about me.
new: I will be gathered with my kind, so I choose my company carefully.
try: Spend some time today with one person who makes you a better Muslim.

title: Guide them now, to the path of Fire.
subtitle: The bitter end of refusing guidance
then: Ibn Kathir explains it as {trap}take them to the way to Hell.{/trap} The word used is guide, the same word as the guidance they turned away from all their lives.
now: Every day you choose what leads you: the next video, a friend's opinion, your mood, or the Quran. {idea}Something is always guiding you.{/idea} The verse asks you to choose that guide now.
old: I am not following anyone; I just do my own thing.
new: I am always being led by something, so I want Allah to be my guide.
try: Say ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim slowly and with meaning in your next prayer.

title: Stop them. They will be questioned.
subtitle: Every life comes with questions

row.title: questioned
sub: about what they did and said

then: Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}detain them, for they are to be brought to account.{/idea} Uthman bin Zaidah said the first thing a man will be asked about is {trap}the company he kept.{/trap}
now: A job interview: they stop you and ask, why did you leave your last job? You need an answer ready. {idea}There will be questions about how you spent your life{/idea}, and you can prepare your answers now.
old: Life just passes, and nobody asks about it.
new: I will be stopped and asked, so I want my answers to be good ones.
try: Before bed, ask yourself one question: how did I spend today? Answer honestly.

title: Why don't you help each other now?
subtitle: Promises of loyalty that vanish
then: Ibn Kathir says this is said {trap}by way of rebuke{/trap}: you claimed you would all help one another. The Quraysh were proud of their tribal loyalty. {trap}On that Day, no tribe will help.{/trap}
now: Your friends say they have your back, the group that always covers for each other's lies at work or at school. {trap}That loyalty has an end date.{/trap} On that Day no one can carry anyone.
old: My friends will always cover for me.
new: Only my deeds and Allah's mercy help me there, so I should not lean on cover-ups.
try: If you are covering for something wrong for a friend, think about how to stop gently.

title: That Day, they simply surrender.
subtitle: When resistance runs out

row.title: surrendered
sub: no way to resist or avoid

then: Ibn Kathir says they will be {trap}subjected to the command of Allah{/trap} and unable to resist or avoid it. People who refused to submit in life will have no choice but to submit then.
now: You argue with every rule: at work, at home, in faith. You hold out. {trap}Eventually everyone gives in to Allah's command.{/trap} {reward}Choosing to give in now is what Islam means.{/reward}
old: Submitting means losing myself.
new: Everyone submits in the end; submitting willingly now is the honour.
try: Pick one command of Allah you resist and follow it today, willingly.

title: They turn to each other, and the blaming starts.
subtitle: Followers and leaders, face to face
then: Ibn Kathir says the disbelievers will {trap}blame one another{/trap} at the Resurrection, as they will argue in Hell. He cites 40:47 and 34:31, where the weak blame the arrogant and the arrogant push it back.
now: Something goes wrong at work and the meeting turns into finger pointing: you said, no you said. {idea}Blame passed around does not make it lighter.{/idea} Each person still owns their part.
old: If someone else talked me into it, it is on them.
new: I own my choices, even the ones others pushed me toward.
try: The next time something goes wrong today, name your own part first.

title: You came at us from the right side.
subtitle: How wrong is made to look right
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {trap}you forced us with your power{/trap}. As-Suddi said you made {trap}falsehood look attractive{/trap} and stopped us seeing the truth. Qatadah said you blocked every good deed.
now: Nobody says, come do something wrong. They say: it is just business, everyone does it, you deserve a treat. {trap}Wrong arrives dressed as right.{/trap} The verse warns you about the right-hand approach.
old: I will know something is wrong because it will look wrong.
new: Wrong often comes looking reasonable, so I look at where it leads.
try: Notice one thing today that is sold to you as harmless. Ask where it actually leads.

title: No, you were never believers yourselves.
subtitle: The leaders throw the blame back
then: Ibn Kathir says the leaders will tell their followers, {trap}it is not as you say; your hearts denied faith{/trap} and were open to disbelief and sin. Those once trusted now turn against them.
now: The friend who got you into a habit is the first to say, I never forced you. And they are partly right. {idea}Someone can open the door, but you walk through it.{/idea}
old: I only went along because of them.
new: Others can invite me, but my heart decides whether to accept.
try: Think of one bad habit you blame on someone else. Own it, and ask Allah for help to leave it.

title: We had no power over you. You were transgressors.
subtitle: No one can force a heart

row.title: you transgressed
sub: you chose us over the prophets

then: Ibn Kathir says the leaders admit: {trap}we had no proof of what we called you to.{/trap} You responded to us and {idea}neglected the truth the prophets brought with proof.{/idea}
now: The influencer you trusted had no evidence, just confidence. The prophets brought clear signs. {idea}You chose who to listen to.{/idea} You can still choose differently.
old: They seemed so sure of themselves, so I followed.
new: Confidence is not proof; I follow those who bring the truth.
try: Unfollow or mute one voice today that pulls you away from Allah.

title: Our Lord's word came true against us.
subtitle: The leaders admit the warning was real
then: Ibn Kathir says the arrogant leaders will tell their followers: {trap}the Word of Allah has been justified against us{/trap}; we are among those who will taste the punishment. {idea}They finally agree with the messengers, but only then.{/idea}
now: You finally admit the doctor was right after the test results come back. You wish you had listened a year earlier. {reward}Agreeing with Allah's word now is still possible{/reward}, and it changes everything.
old: I will believe it when I see it.
new: Agreeing with the truth before I see it is what makes faith worth something.
try: Say one thing Allah told you that you have been slow to accept, and accept it out loud.

title: We misled you because we were lost ourselves.
subtitle: The blind leading the blind
then: Ibn Kathir says the leaders admit: {trap}we called you to follow the path we were on, and you responded.{/trap} They were not hiding a secret truth. {trap}They were simply lost and took others with them.{/trap}
now: The cousin who gives you life advice while his own life is falling apart. The online coach selling a method that did not work for him. {idea}Ask where your guide is actually going.{/idea}
old: Anyone who talks confidently probably knows the way.
new: Before following someone, I check whether they are on the right path themselves.
try: Think of one person whose advice you follow. Ask honestly whether their path leads to Allah.

title: Leaders and followers share the same end.
subtitle: Following does not reduce the cost

row.title: I only followed
sub: so I am off the hook

then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}all of them will be in Hell, each according to what he deserves.{/trap} The blaming in the verses before changes nothing. Leader and follower both carry their part.
now: A group at work cuts corners on a safety check. The manager said to; you went along. When it goes wrong, the report names you both. {idea}Going along is also a choice.{/idea}
old: If I was only following orders, the blame is not mine.
new: Following is a choice too, and I am responsible for mine.
try: If you are asked to go along with something wrong today, politely say no once.

title: This is how We deal with those who do wrong.
subtitle: A fixed rule, not a mood
then: After the scene of leaders and followers sharing the punishment, Allah states the rule: {idea}this is how We deal with criminals.{/idea} Ibn Kathir ties it to the next verse, which explains their real crime: {trap}arrogance.{/trap}
now: You know the rules of your workplace: be late three times and you get a warning. It is not personal; it is the system. {idea}Allah's justice is consistent{/idea}, and {reward}so is His mercy to those who turn back.{/reward}
old: Maybe I will be the exception.
new: Allah's way is consistent, so I can rely on it: turn back and His mercy is there.
try: Make istighfar a few times today, trusting His rule that He forgives those who ask.

title: Told there is no god but Allah, they puffed up with pride.
subtitle: The real reason they refused
then: Ibn Kathir says that in this world {trap}they were too arrogant to say these words{/trap} as the believers said them. The problem was not the words. {trap}It was what saying them would cost their pride.{/trap}
now: Sometimes you know you are wrong in an argument, but saying "you are right" feels impossible. {trap}Pride locks your mouth.{/trap} {idea}La ilaha illallah is the biggest "You are right" there is.{/idea}
old: I would accept the truth if it were clear enough.
new: Often what stops me is not doubt but pride.
try: Say La ilaha illallah slowly ten times today, meaning it as a bow of the heart.

title: Leave our gods for a mad poet? they said.
subtitle: Insulting the messenger to keep the habit

row.title: "a mad poet"
sub: their name for the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: attack the messenger
sub: so the message can be ignored

then: Ibn Kathir explains their words: {trap}shall we stop worshipping our gods and our forefathers' gods{/trap} because of this mad poet? They meant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Insulting him was easier than leaving their tradition.
now: Someone gives you good advice and you think: who is he to tell me, he is younger than me, he is not even that religious. {trap}You go after the speaker to avoid the message.{/trap}
old: If I can find a fault in the person, I can ignore what they said.
new: The truth stays true whoever says it, so I listen to the message.
try: Think of one piece of advice you dismissed because of who said it. Reconsider it today.

title: No. He brought the truth and confirmed the messengers.
subtitle: Allah's reply to the insult
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ {idea}brought the truth{/idea}, and confirmed the earlier messengers by {reward}fulfilling their prophecies{/reward} about him. He links it to 41:43: nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you.
now: When you feel your faith is old-fashioned or out of step, remember: {idea}it is the oldest message there is{/idea}, carried by Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and finally Muhammad ﷺ. You are part of a long line.
old: My faith is just one opinion among many.
new: I carry the same truth every messenger brought; it is not new and not strange.
try: Read the story of one earlier prophet in the Quran this week and notice the shared message.

title: You will taste a painful punishment.
subtitle: The warning said directly to the deniers
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is {trap}addressing the people{/trap} directly here. It comes right after the Quraysh called the Prophet ﷺ a mad poet. Then an exception follows for His sincere servants.
now: You hear a warning in a talk and immediately think of someone else who needs it. {idea}The verse is speaking to whoever hears it{/idea}, which right now is you. {reward}And the next verses open a door.{/reward}
old: Warnings like this are for really bad people.
new: Every warning is for me to check myself, and there is a way out.
try: When you hear a warning today, apply it to yourself before anyone else.

title: Repaid only for what you used to do.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing invented

row.title: it is excessive
sub: too much for what I did

then: Ibn Kathir quotes it together with the verse before: {idea}you will be requited nothing except for what you used to do.{/idea} The same rule appeared in Ya-Sin (36:54). No one is punished for what they did not do.
now: You keep a running list of others' faults but go easy on your own. {idea}The scale only weighs your own deeds{/idea}, not your cousin's or your coworker's. That is where your attention belongs.
old: I am not as bad as a lot of people.
new: I will be weighed on my own deeds, not compared with others.
try: Tonight, list one thing you did well and one to fix tomorrow. Only about yourself.

title: Except Allah's sincere servants.
subtitle: The exception that changes everything
then: Ibn Kathir compares this to Surah Al-Asr: man is in loss {reward}except those who believe and do good{/reward}. For the sincere, {reward}their evil acts, if any, are overlooked{/reward}, and each good deed is multiplied ten to seven hundred times.
now: You worry you are not good enough: you miss prayers, you lose your temper. {reward}The exception is not for the flawless.{/reward} It is for those whose hearts belong to Allah and keep coming back.
old: Only perfect people are saved.
new: Sincerity is what Allah looks for, and He overlooks much for the sincere.
try: Do one deed today purely for Allah, and tell no one about it.

title: For them, a known provision.
subtitle: Provision that is certain, not hoped for
then: Qatadah and As-Suddi said {reward}this means Paradise.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says the next verse explains it further. For people in Makkah who were often short of food and safety, a provision that was {reward}known and certain{/reward} meant a great deal.
now: Payday is three days away and the account is almost empty. You do the maths again and again. {reward}The provision promised to the sincere is fixed, already known.{/reward} No maths needed.
old: Provision is always uncertain; I never know if there will be enough.
new: The provision that matters most is already set aside for the sincere.
try: When you worry about money today, say: my provision is with Allah. Then do one sensible thing.

title: Fruits, and they are honoured.
subtitle: Gifts given with respect
then: Ibn Kathir says the fruits are {reward}of different kinds{/reward}, and honoured means {reward}they will be served{/reward} and live in luxury. Many early believers in Makkah were poor or enslaved, treated with no respect at all.
now: You do a thankless job: cleaning, caring for a parent, working nights in a hospital. Nobody serves you; you serve everyone. {reward}There is a place where you will be the honoured guest.{/reward}
old: People like me are never the ones who get honoured.
new: Allah has honour waiting for His sincere servants, however unseen they are now.
try: Honour one person today who is usually overlooked: thank them by name.

title: In gardens of pleasure.
subtitle: Where the sincere finally live
then: Ibn Kathir reads this with the next verse: {reward}in the Gardens of Delight, facing one another on thrones.{/reward} For people in a dry, rocky valley, gardens were the clearest picture of a good life.
now: You scroll through photos of holiday villas and dream houses. You save for a better flat. {reward}The home being described here is better than every picture on your screen{/reward}, and it lasts.
old: A nicer home here would finally make me content.
new: My real home is the Gardens of Delight; here I am only passing through.
try: Make dua today, by name, for Jannat an-Naim for yourself and your family.

title: On thrones, facing one another.
subtitle: No one turns their back on anyone
then: Mujahid said: {reward}one of them will not look at another's back.{/reward} Everyone sits facing each other. There are no cold shoulders and no one left out of the circle.
now: Two brothers who have not spoken for a year sit at the same family dinner, turned away from each other. {trap}A turned back says everything.{/trap} {reward}In Paradise, nobody's back is turned.{/reward}
old: Some people I just will not face again.
new: Paradise is face to face, so I can start mending things here.
try: Send a short, kind message to someone you have been giving the cold shoulder.

title: A cup passed around from a flowing spring.
subtitle: A drink that never runs out
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}refined the drink of Paradise{/reward} from the harms of this world's wine. It comes from {reward}a flowing stream they do not fear will ever cease.{/reward} The next verses describe its purity.
now: Every good thing here has an end: the holiday, the weekend, the last slice, the visit. You start missing it before it is over. {reward}There, the good things flow and do not stop.{/reward}
old: Every good thing has to end.
new: In Paradise, the good things keep flowing with no end.
try: Enjoy one simple drink today slowly, and thank Allah for it.

title: Bright white, and delicious to drink.
subtitle: Pleasure with nothing ugly in it

row.title: delicious
sub: taste as good as its look

then: Zayd bin Aslam said it is {reward}white flowing{/reward}, a bright shining colour, unlike this world's drinks that a sound nature finds repulsive. Ibn Kathir says {reward}its taste will be as good as its colour.{/reward}
now: The energy drink tastes great and leaves you shaky. The late-night snack feels good and you regret it at 2am. {trap}So many pleasures here come with a bill.{/trap} {reward}This one does not.{/reward}
old: Every pleasure has a downside I have to accept.
new: Allah has pleasure waiting that has no downside at all.
try: Skip one pleasure today that you know leaves you feeling worse afterwards.

title: No headache, no losing your mind.
subtitle: Joy that keeps you clear
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said ghawl means {trap}stomach aches and such effects{/trap}. Mujahid said it {reward}will not cause them to lose their minds.{/reward} Ibn Abbas listed four harms of this world's wine; Paradise's drink is free of all of them.
now: You come home exhausted and want to switch off: hours of scrolling, numbing out. You wake up foggier. {reward}The joy of Paradise does not take you away from yourself.{/reward} It makes you more awake.
old: Real relaxation means switching my mind off.
new: The best joy keeps me clear and present, not numb.
try: Replace twenty minutes of numbing out tonight with something that leaves you clear: a walk, a call, some Quran.

title: Companions whose eyes are for them alone.
subtitle: Loyalty as part of the reward
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said these are {reward}chaste companions who will not look at anyone other than their husbands.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says their eyes are described as {reward}beautiful and chaste{/reward} together.
now: Your phone is full of images built to pull your eyes away from the person beside you. {idea}Here, the picture of beauty is a gaze that stays faithful.{/idea} Guarding your own gaze is part of that beauty now.
old: Where my eyes wander does not hurt anyone.
new: A faithful gaze is part of what Allah calls beautiful, and I can practise it now.
try: Lower your gaze once today when you notice it wandering, and say astaghfirullah.

title: Like well-protected, untouched pearls.
subtitle: Something precious kept safe
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {reward}as if they were hidden pearls{/reward}. Al-Hasan said protected, {reward}never touched by any hands.{/reward} Others said the inside of an egg, beneath the shell, which no hand reaches.
now: You keep your most precious things somewhere safe: the ring in a box, documents in a drawer, not left on the bus seat. {reward}What is precious is protected.{/reward} That applies to your heart and your dignity too.
old: Something is only valuable if everyone can see it.
new: The most precious things are guarded, and that care is part of their worth.
try: Keep one private thing private today that you might have posted or shared.

title: In Paradise, friends turn to each other and talk.
subtitle: Remembering the road that got them there

row.title: their stories
sub: how life was, what they suffered

then: Ibn Kathir says the people of Paradise will ask one another {reward}how they were in this world and what they suffered{/reward}, while they sit together and servants bring them delights no eye has seen.
now: You are in the middle of a hard year: the job loss, the illness, the long nights. {reward}One day it may be a story you tell, smiling, among friends in the gardens.{/reward} Today is a chapter, not the ending.
old: What I am going through now is just pointless pain.
new: The hard parts of my life can become stories of how Allah carried me.
try: Tell one friend today about a hard time Allah helped you through.

title: I had a companion back in the world.
subtitle: A memory of a friend who doubted
then: Ibn Abbas said this refers to {idea}an idolator man who had a believing companion{/idea} in this world. Ibn Kathir also mentions a report of two business partners: one spent on himself, the other gave in charity.
now: You think of your oldest friends: the one from school, the colleague you lunch with every day. {idea}Each of them is quietly pulling you in a direction.{/idea} One day you will remember which way.
old: My friendships do not affect my faith.
new: My companions shape my path, so I choose and influence them with care.
try: Think of one friend you love who doubts. Make a sincere dua for them by name.

title: He kept asking: you really believe all this?
subtitle: The quiet pressure of a doubting friend
then: Ibn Kathir says he asked whether his friend believed in {idea}the resurrection, the Reckoning, and reward{/idea}, and said it {trap}by way of astonishment, disbelief and stubbornness.{/trap}
now: Lunch at work. Someone says, wait, you actually believe in all that? Everyone looks at you. {trap}The question is light; the pressure is heavy.{/trap} The believer in this story held on.
old: If smart people around me find it strange, maybe it is.
new: A friend's surprise is not an argument; I can stay firm and kind.
try: If someone questions your faith today, answer calmly with one sentence you truly believe.

title: Once we are dust, we will be held to account?
subtitle: The doubt that deeds really count
then: Mujahid and As-Suddi said madinun means {idea}brought to account.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said {idea}rewarded or punished according to our deeds.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says both views are correct.
now: You cheat a little on expenses and think: who will ever know, it is tiny. You help a stranger and think: it does not really matter. {idea}Both get counted.{/idea}
old: Small things do not really count in the end.
new: Every deed, small or big, is brought to account.
try: Do one small honest thing today that no one would notice if you skipped it.

title: Would you like to look?
subtitle: A believer wonders where his friend ended up
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer {idea}says this to his companions among the people of Paradise{/idea}: will you look over? He remembers his old friend and wants to know where he is.
now: You scroll through old contacts and wonder what happened to people you once spent every day with. {idea}Close friends can end up in very different places.{/idea} The path you walk together matters.
old: We will always be close, whatever we each believe.
new: Friends can end up far apart, so I want to walk with mine toward Allah.
try: Invite one friend to something good this week: a class, a prayer, a charity visit.

title: He looked, and saw him in the middle of the Fire.
subtitle: The friend's choice reached its end
then: Ibn Abbas and others said it means {trap}in the middle of Hell.{/trap} The two had been companions in the world. Their paths split over one question: {idea}do you believe in the meeting with Allah?{/idea}
now: Two kids sit at the same school desk. Same teacher, same chances. Twenty years later, one built a good life, one lost his way. {idea}Small choices, repeated, decide the end.{/idea} Yours are still being made.
old: We are friends, so we will end up the same way.
new: My own choices decide my end, whoever I sit beside.
try: Make one choice today you would be glad to look back on.

title: By Allah, you almost ruined me.
subtitle: How close the danger really was
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer tells the disbeliever: {trap}by Allah, you nearly caused me to be doomed, if I had obeyed you.{/trap} Only now does he see how close the danger was.
now: The friend who said, come on, just this once. The group that almost pulled you in. Looking back, you shiver at how close it was. {trap}Some influences nearly cost us everything.{/trap}
old: I would never have fallen for that.
new: I was closer to the edge than I knew, and I need to watch who pulls on me.
try: Name one influence that almost pulled you away from Allah. Thank Him for saving you.

title: If not for my Lord's favour, I would be there too.
subtitle: Guidance as a gift, not an achievement
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer means: {reward}He bestowed His grace upon me, had mercy upon me and guided me to faith.{/reward} He links it to 7:43: we could never have found guidance had Allah not guided us.
now: You see someone struggling with addiction or anger and feel a little proud that you are not like them. {reward}Your steadiness is a gift.{/reward} Without His favour, it could be you.
old: I am on the right path because I made good choices.
new: I am guided because Allah was kind to me, so I stay humble and thankful.
try: When you see someone struggling today, say alhamdulillah quietly and make dua for them.

title: So we will never die again?
subtitle: The joy of a life with no ending
then: Ibn Kathir says the believers say this {reward}when they feel joy{/reward} at what Allah has given them, realising they will remain forever. Al-Hasan said: {trap}they know that death ends every delight{/trap}, so they ask.
now: Even on your happiest day, at a wedding, holding a newborn, a small voice says: this will not last. {trap}Every joy here has an edge.{/trap} {reward}In Paradise the edge is gone.{/reward}
old: Every happy moment is shadowed by knowing it will end.
new: There is a happiness coming that never has to end.
try: In a happy moment today, say: O Allah, give me the joy that never ends.

title: Only that first death, and no punishment.
subtitle: The worst is behind them forever
then: Ibn Kathir says the believers realise {reward}they are to remain in Paradise forever, with no punishment and no death to come.{/reward} The only death they will ever know is the one already behind them.
now: You lie awake some nights afraid of dying, of losing your parents, of the hospital corridor. {reward}For the believer, death is one door, walked through once.{/reward} After that, never again.
old: Death is the thing I fear most.
new: For the believer, death is one door, and what lies past it is safety.
try: When the fear of death comes today, say: O Allah, make my last day my best day.

title: This is the great success.
subtitle: What winning actually means
then: Al-Hasan said that when they ask whether they will die again, {reward}it will be said: no, truly this is the supreme success.{/reward} Ibn Kathir reads the next verse with it: {idea}for the like of this, let the workers work.{/idea}
now: Your LinkedIn says success is a new title. Your feed says it is a car or a holiday. You chase it every day. {reward}The verse names the real win{/reward}, and every small good deed is work toward it.
old: Success is what I can show people now.
new: The great success is Paradise, and I work for it in small ways every day.
try: Write down one goal for this week that works toward the great success, and start it today.

title: This is what all the effort was for.
subtitle: The finish line that makes the work worth it
then: In Paradise, a believer has just seen what happened to the friend who mocked the resurrection. He thanks his Lord and says there is no more death for them. Then comes the line Ibn Jarir calls the Words of Allah: {idea}for the like of this, let the workers work.{/idea}
now: You stay late for the promotion. You save for years for the house. You train months for one race. {trap}All of it ends, and you know it ends.{/trap} This verse points at the one goal that does not, and says: put your effort there too.
old: I work hard for things I can see and hold.
new: The best place to aim my effort is the success that never ends.
try: Pick one task you already do today and quietly set your intention for it to be for Allah.

title: Two tables are set. Which is the better welcome?
subtitle: A question put to the listener, not just told
then: After describing the delights of Paradise, Allah turns and asks a question. Is that the better welcome, or {trap}the tree of Zaqqum{/trap}, a specific tree in Hell? The Quraysh who mocked the message heard it as a question meant for them.
now: Nobody would choose the bad table if it were laid out in front of them. But the choice is not made at the table. {idea}It is made in small moments{/idea}: the reply you send, the hour you give, the thing you do when no one is watching.
old: Of course I would choose Paradise. That is obvious.
new: The answer is not in what I say I want, but in what I keep choosing.
try: Before one decision today, ask yourself which table this choice walks toward.

title: The same news became a test of how people listen.
subtitle: Mocking what you cannot picture

row.title: the One who made fire
sub: can make what lives in it

then: Qatadah said the mockers argued: {trap}your companion says there is a tree in the Fire, but fire consumes trees.{/trap} Mujahid reports Abu Jahl joked that Zaqqum was just dates and butter. Ibn Kathir says the tree was mentioned {idea}as a trial, to show who would believe{/idea}.
now: You read a verse about the unseen and your first thought is: that makes no sense. You could laugh it off like a meme in the group chat. {idea}Or you could notice the limit is in your picture, not in Allah.{/idea}
old: If I cannot imagine it, it probably is not real.
new: My imagination is small. How I respond to what I cannot picture is the real test.
try: Next time a verse puzzles you, write the question down and look it up instead of brushing it off.

title: A tree whose roots drink from the fire.
subtitle: What grows depends on its soil
then: This verse answers the joke. Qatadah explained that the tree grows from the very bottom of Hell and {idea}is nourished by the fire, for it was created from fire{/idea}. The objection that fire burns trees does not apply to a tree made for it.
now: Some things in your life only grow because of bad soil. {trap}The grudge that lives on every new slight.{/trap} The habit that feeds on stress. Pull the root and the tree has nothing to drink.
old: Things happen the way I am used to seeing them happen.
new: Allah makes each thing fit the place He made it for.
try: Name one bad habit and the feeling it feeds on. Cut off that feeding once today.

title: Its fruit looks like the ugliest thing you can imagine.
subtitle: A picture built from what people already feel
then: Ibn Kathir explains this describes how ugly the tree is. It is compared to the heads of devils, {idea}even though no one has seen them{/idea}, because people already carry a fixed idea that devils are ugly. The image works on the listener's own sense of disgust.
now: Sin rarely looks ugly from the front. It shows up as a good deal, a harmless joke, a quick look. {trap}The verse lets you see the fruit at the end of the branch{/trap}, so the attraction loses its shine.
old: If something looks harmless now, it probably is.
new: Look at what a thing turns into, not how it is packaged.
try: Think of one temptation you know well. Picture where it ends, then let that picture speak when it comes.

title: They fill their bellies, and it never feeds them.
subtitle: Eating only because nothing else is left
then: Ibn Kathir says they will eat from this ugly tree {trap}because they will find nothing else to eat{/trap}. He links it to another verse: food that neither nourishes nor helps against hunger. It was a warning to Quraysh while there was still time.
now: Even here you know what it is to fill up on things that do not feed you. {trap}Hours of scrolling, and you feel emptier.{/trap} A purchase that is forgotten by Friday. {idea}This life is where you still get to choose what nourishes you.{/idea}
old: As long as I am full, I am fine.
new: What I fill myself with now matters, while the choice is still mine.
try: Swap ten minutes of something empty today for ten minutes of something that nourishes you.

title: After the food comes the drink, and it is no mercy.
subtitle: The welcome of verse 62 turned inside out
then: Verse 62 asked which welcome is better. Here the answer continues: after eating Zaqqum, Ibn 'Abbas said, {trap}they will be given boiling water to drink{/trap}. The order of a meal, food and then drink, is kept, but nothing in it brings relief.
now: A good host brings water after the meal without being asked. You know that small kindness from your mother's kitchen. {idea}Paradise is that, without end.{/idea} The verse asks you to want the right host, and to live toward His house.
old: Warnings about the next life are too far away to affect today.
new: The meal I am heading toward is shaped by the choices I make at today's table.
try: Offer someone a drink or a meal today with real care, and think of the welcome you hope for.

title: Then they are sent back, with no way out of the circle.
subtitle: A cycle that no longer has an exit
then: Ibn Kathir explains that after the drink {trap}they are returned to the burning fire{/trap}, rotating between the two, and links it to 55:44. Ibn Mas'ud added that by midday of that Day, everyone will already be settled in their place.
now: You know loops: the same argument every holiday, the same relapse every month, the same promise every Monday. {idea}Here, every loop still has a door.{/idea} Repentance is that door, and it is open today.
old: I will fix this pattern later. There is always time.
new: Right now, unlike then, every cycle in my life can still be broken.
try: Name one repeating mistake. Do one thing differently the next time it starts.

title: They found their fathers lost, and never asked why.
subtitle: Inheriting a path without checking it
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the reason for what came before: they found their fathers on misguidance and {trap}followed them with no evidence or proof{/trap}. The Quraysh used exactly this argument against the Prophet ﷺ.
now: Every family hands down habits. How money is talked about, how anger is shown, which relatives you do not speak to. {idea}Some are gifts. Some need checking.{/idea} Loving your parents does not mean copying every step.
old: This is how my family has always done it, so it is right.
new: I honor my parents best by keeping what is true and checking the rest.
try: Pick one habit you got from home and ask honestly: would I choose this if I saw it fresh?

title: They did not walk in those footsteps. They ran.
subtitle: Rushing to copy without a pause
then: Mujahid said the word means something like running. Sa'id bin Jubayr said {trap}they followed ignorance and foolishness{/trap}. They were not dragged into the old path. They rushed to it.
now: A trend starts and within a day everyone is doing it. The group chat agrees, so you agree. {trap}Speed feels like certainty.{/trap} {idea}The pause is where your own mind gets a say.{/idea}
old: If everyone is moving fast in one direction, they must know something.
new: Rushing after others is often a way of not thinking. A pause is a kind of freedom.
try: Before you share, buy, or join something today, wait five minutes and ask where it leads.

title: Most people before them went astray too.
subtitle: Numbers are not proof
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us that {trap}most of the previous nations went astray{/trap}, worshipping other gods alongside Him. For the small, persecuted group of Muslims in Makkah, this was comfort: being few was nothing new.
now: You are the only one at the office who does not join in. The only one in the family who prays on time. It feels lonely, and you wonder if you are wrong. {idea}Being outnumbered has never decided what is true.{/idea}
old: If most people do it, it is probably fine.
new: Most people have been wrong before. I check the path, not the crowd.
try: Think of one good thing you do that few around you do. Keep doing it today, quietly.

title: No one was left without a warning.
subtitle: Allah sent warners to every lost people
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}sent warners among them to alert them{/idea} to His anger toward those who worship others. The warning came first. What followed was their own persistence in opposing the Messengers.
now: Warnings come in small sizes too. A friend who says you have changed. A verse that lands at the exact wrong moment. A scare at the doctor's office. {idea}Each one is a kindness, sent before it is too late.{/idea}
old: Nobody ever really told me this was wrong.
new: Reminders keep arriving. The question is whether I treat them as gifts.
try: Recall one reminder someone gave you that you ignored. Thank them, or act on it today.

title: Look at how it ended for those who were warned.
subtitle: Judge a path by its end
then: Ibn Kathir says the nations {trap}persisted in opposing their Messengers{/trap}, so Allah destroyed those who disbelieved and saved the believers. Quraysh are told to look at that history and see themselves in it.
now: Every shortcut looks good at the start. The loan you cannot afford, the lie that gets you out of trouble, the friend you drop for a better crowd. {idea}The verse says: look at the end first.{/idea}
old: Right now it is working, so it must be fine.
new: A path is measured by where it ends, not how it feels at the start.
try: Before one choice today, picture how it looks a year from now. Let that decide.

title: Except the ones who were sincerely His.
subtitle: The exception inside every warning
then: The warning about past nations has a door in it. Allah {reward}saved the believers and caused them to prevail{/reward}. They are called His chosen, sincere servants, devoted to Him alone.
now: Whenever you hear a hard warning, look for the word except. It is always there for the one who turns back to Allah with a sincere heart. {idea}You can be in that exception, starting today.{/idea}
old: Warnings like this are just about other people.
new: Every warning has an exception, and sincerity is how I enter it.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about. Keep it just for Allah.

title: Nuh called after centuries, and the Best Answerer answered.
subtitle: A tired prayer after a long struggle
then: This begins the story of Nuh in detail. He stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty, and every call pushed them further away. Then he prayed, {idea}I have been overcome, so help me.{/idea} Allah says: We are the best of those who answer.
now: Years of trying with a family member who will not change. Years at a job that does not improve. You feel embarrassed to admit you are worn out. {idea}Nuh's prayer was just that: I have nothing left.{/idea} And it was answered.
old: I should not complain to Allah. I should just keep going.
new: Telling Allah honestly that I am overcome is a prayer He answers.
try: Tonight, tell Allah in your own words exactly where you feel overcome. Ask for help by name.

title: Rescued from the weight of being mocked for so long.
subtitle: The great distress was their rejection and insults
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the great distress here means {trap}their disbelief and their insults{/trap}. Nuh and the few with him lived under that weight for centuries. Allah took it seriously enough to call it great, and rescued them.
now: The relative who makes fun of your prayer at every family dinner. The coworkers who roll their eyes when you skip the drinks. {idea}Allah does not treat that pressure as small.{/idea} He sees it, and He is the one who lifts it.
old: Being mocked is not a real hardship. I should just ignore it.
new: Allah counts the weight of being mocked for faith, and He rescues from it.
try: If someone mocks your faith today, answer kindly once, then hand the hurt to Allah in a short du'a.

title: The few who believed became the ancestors of everyone.
subtitle: His descendants were the ones who remained
then: Ibn 'Abbas said no one was left except the offspring of Nuh, and Qatadah said {reward}all people descended from them{/reward}. A hadith in At-Tirmidhi names his sons Sam, Ham and Yafith. The crowd that laughed at him left no line.
now: The bus, the hospital waiting room, the stranger in the queue: every one of them is your distant cousin through Nuh's family. {idea}No one you meet is truly a stranger.{/idea}
old: People unlike me are a different kind of people.
new: Everyone I meet shares an ancestor with me who stayed faithful.
try: Be warm today to one stranger you would usually ignore. Think of them as family.

title: The world stopped mocking him and started praising him.
subtitle: A good name left among later generations
then: Ibn 'Abbas said Nuh {reward}is remembered in a good way{/reward}. Mujahid said it means an honorable mention by all the Prophets. The man his own people insulted for centuries is the one whose name is spoken with respect.
now: Your reputation at work, your followers, what the family says about you behind your back. You spend a lot of energy managing it. {idea}The good name that lasts is the one Allah leaves for you{/idea}, and it comes from what you did when no one clapped.
old: I need people to think well of me right now.
new: The name worth having is the one Allah leaves after I am gone.
try: Do one good thing today you would never post or mention.

title: Peace on Nuh, from every people in every age.
subtitle: The greeting that every nation gives him
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse explains how far the honorable mention reaches: {reward}he is greeted with peace by all groups and nations{/reward}. The man who once had almost no one now has everyone.
now: Every time you say peace be upon him after Nuh's name, you are part of this verse coming true. {idea}A greeting can be an act of honor.{/idea} The words you add after a name carry weight.
old: Saying peace be upon him is just a habit.
new: When I greet the Prophets with peace, I join a promise Allah made.
try: Say peace be upon him with attention the next time you hear a Prophet's name.

title: This is how Allah repays those who do good.
subtitle: The reward that comes after the struggle
then: Ibn Kathir says this means: {reward}this is how We reward those of Our servants who obey Allah{/reward}. Nuh was given an honorable mention so that after his death he is still remembered as he deserves.
now: You give in charity and nothing changes. You stay patient with a difficult parent and get no thanks. {idea}The verse says thus, meaning this is a pattern, not a one-time event.{/idea} Your good is not lost.
old: If doing good does not pay off soon, it was wasted.
new: Allah has a set way of repaying good. It is never wasted, only timed.
try: Keep doing one good thing today that has not paid off yet. Tell yourself: this is noted.

title: His highest title: one of Our believing servants.
subtitle: What Allah chose to call Nuh
then: After all the honor, Allah sums Nuh up simply. Ibn Kathir explains it means {idea}one of the sincere believers in the Oneness of Allah, one of those who had certain faith{/idea}.
now: Your profile lists your job title, degree, and city. Your family introduces you by your achievements. {idea}The title Allah gives His best people is servant.{/idea} It is open to you too, whatever your CV says.
old: My worth is my titles and achievements.
new: The best title I can carry is a believing servant of Allah.
try: Before you introduce yourself today, quietly remind yourself: first, I am His servant.

title: Then the others were drowned, and left no trace.
subtitle: The mockers are remembered only by this
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah destroyed them and {trap}there was no trace whatsoever left of them{/trap}. They are known only by this unfavorable description. For the small Muslim group in Makkah, the contrast spoke directly to their situation.
now: Every age has its loud voices that seem permanent. The verse is not asking you to point at anyone. {idea}It asks which side of your own story you are writing{/idea}, in how you treat truth and the people who carry it.
old: Whoever is loudest now will be the one remembered.
new: Only what stands with the truth lasts. I want my part of the story there.
try: Think of one moment where you joined in mocking something good. Seek forgiveness and do the opposite today.

title: Ibrahim walked the same road Nuh walked.
subtitle: One path carried across generations
then: Ibn 'Abbas said Ibrahim {idea}was one of the followers of Nuh's religion{/idea}. Mujahid said he was following his path and his way. The story moves from one Prophet to the next, showing it is one message.
now: Some days you feel like the only person trying. The only one in your class, or your office, keeping your prayers. {idea}You are not starting something new.{/idea} You are walking a road Nuh and Ibrahim already walked.
old: I am on my own in trying to live my faith.
new: I stand in a long line of people who walked this same way.
try: Read the story of one Prophet today and notice what you share with him.

title: He came to his Lord with a sound heart.
subtitle: The heart that is free from shirk
then: Ibn 'Abbas said a sound heart means bearing witness that none deserves worship but Allah. Ibn Sirin described it as {idea}one that knows Allah is true, the Hour will come, and the dead will be raised{/idea}. Al-Hasan said: free from shirk.
now: Your heart is pulled every day by worry about money, by what people think, by the next notification. {trap}A lot of things compete for the top spot.{/trap} A sound heart is not one with no worries. It is one where Allah stays first.
old: As long as I believe in Allah, my heart is fine.
new: A sound heart keeps Allah first even when many things pull at it.
try: Notice the first thing your heart turns to when you wake tomorrow. Turn it to Allah instead.

title: He asked his own father one honest question.
subtitle: What is it you are worshipping?
then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {idea}denounced his people for their worship of idols and false gods{/idea}. He began with a question, and he asked it of the closest person to him, his own father, along with his people.
now: It is hard to raise something with your own parents. Easier to keep the peace at the dinner table. {idea}A gentle, honest question can open a door that a lecture slams shut.{/idea}
old: I cannot raise hard things with my family. It will only cause trouble.
new: A respectful, honest question can be the bravest thing I say at home.
try: Ask yourself the question first: what do I actually give my devotion to? Write the honest answer.

title: You want a lie for a god instead of Allah?
subtitle: False gods are something people choose
then: Ibrahim's second question names it plainly: {trap}a falsehood, gods besides Allah, that you desire{/trap}. The word points at wanting. The idols were not forced on them. They were preferred.
now: Sometimes you know the truth but want something else more. The extra hour on the phone instead of prayer. The deal that is a little dishonest. {trap}It is not confusion. It is wanting.{/trap} {idea}Naming the want is the first step out.{/idea}
old: I just did not know better.
new: Often I do know. The honest question is what I want more than Allah.
try: Name one thing you knowingly put before Allah this week. Put it second, once, today.

title: What do you think the Lord of the worlds will do?
subtitle: Your idea of Allah shapes how you live
then: Qatadah explained Ibrahim's question as: {idea}what do you think He will do with you when you meet Him{/idea}, given that you worshipped others alongside Him? It turns the argument from idols to their own meeting with Allah.
now: What you assume about Allah shows in your week. If you think He does not notice, you cut corners. If you know He is Lord of everything, generous and just, you live differently. {idea}Your idea of Him is steering you.{/idea}
old: Allah is forgiving, so it does not really matter what I do.
new: What I expect from my meeting with Allah should shape what I do today.
try: Spend two minutes today thinking about meeting Allah. Ask what you want to bring.

title: He looked up at the stars and thought.
subtitle: A pause to plan before acting
then: Qatadah said {idea}the Arabs say of one who thinks deeply that he is looking at the stars{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim looked up while thinking of a way to stay behind when his people went out to their festival.
now: Before the hard conversation, the big decision, the reply to the angry email: you look out the window for a minute. {idea}That pause is not wasted time.{/idea} It is where the wise move gets found.
old: Thinking first is just delaying.
new: A quiet pause to think is part of acting well.
try: Before one reaction today, step away for one minute and think it through.

title: I am sick, he said, and he meant it.
subtitle: Sick at heart of what his people worshipped
then: His people wanted him to join their festival. Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {idea}told them something that was true, for he was indeed sick of what they believed in{/idea}. One explanation is that he meant: I am sick at heart of your worshipping idols instead of Allah.
now: Your friends are heading to something you do not want to be part of. You do not need a speech or a fight. {idea}A short, truthful no is enough{/idea}, and it leaves you free for what matters.
old: To step out, I have to argue or make a scene.
new: I can step away from wrong with a short, honest word.
try: If you are invited to something you should skip today, decline briefly and truthfully.

title: The crowd left, and he stayed with a purpose.
subtitle: When everyone walks away, you choose what to do
then: His people {trap}turned away from him and departed{/trap} for their festival. Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim then went to the idols after they had left, quickly and secretly. Being left alone gave him the moment he needed.
now: Everyone is at the party, and the photos fill your phone. You are home. {idea}That empty evening can be the one where you finally pray long, read, or fix what you have been putting off.{/idea}
old: If I am left out, I am losing something.
new: Being left alone can be the space Allah gives me to do what matters.
try: Use one quiet hour this week, when others are busy elsewhere, for something you have long delayed.

title: Food set before gods that cannot eat.
subtitle: Offerings to things that cannot receive
then: Ibn Kathir says the people {trap}had placed food before the idols as a sacrifice, so that the food might be blessed{/trap}. When Ibrahim saw it, he asked them: will you not eat? The question showed how helpless they were.
now: You give your best hours to things that give nothing back. The lucky charm on the mirror, the brand you trust more than your prayer. {idea}Ask them: can you actually do anything for me?{/idea}
old: Some things bring luck or blessing on their own.
new: Only Allah gives blessing. Everything else needs Him as much as I do.
try: Notice one thing you treat as lucky or protective. Remind yourself today that blessing is from Allah alone.

title: Why do you not answer? They had nothing to say.
subtitle: A god that cannot speak cannot guide

key.label: What you should ask of a god

then: Standing alone among the idols, Ibrahim asked {idea}what is the matter with you that you speak not?{/idea} The food sat untouched. The statues stayed silent. Their silence was the whole argument.
now: In the hospital corridor, your savings, your connections, your title cannot say a word to you. {idea}Allah hears the whisper you cannot even say out loud.{/idea} Turn to the One who answers.
old: What I rely on will be there for me when it counts.
new: Only Allah hears and answers. Everything else goes silent when I need it most.
try: Next time you are worried today, speak to Allah first before reaching for anything else.

title: He struck the idols with his strong right hand.
subtitle: Breaking what had been worshipped

key.label: How to deal with an idol

then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {idea}hit them with his right hand because it is stronger{/idea}, and left them broken to pieces, except the biggest, so the people might turn to it. The full story is told in Surat Al-Anbiya'.
now: You do not need to break anyone else's things. Look at your own idols: the app that owns your nights, the habit that comes before prayer. {idea}Half measures keep it standing.{/idea} Use your strong hand.
old: I will cut back slowly on what pulls me from Allah.
new: Some things in my life need a decisive break, not a slow negotiation.
try: Remove one thing today that keeps pulling you from Allah. Delete it, give it away, or block it.

title: The crowd came rushing back at him.
subtitle: When you break with the group, the group comes
then: Mujahid said the word means {trap}they came rushing{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes they did not know at first who had done it, until they looked into it and found it was Ibrahim. Then they came to rebuke him.
now: You stop joining in the gossip, and suddenly the group chat goes quiet, then turns on you. {trap}Everyone wants an explanation.{/trap} {idea}You do not have to panic. You can answer calmly and stay where you are.{/idea}
old: If many people come at me, I must have done something wrong.
new: Pressure from many does not make the truth wrong. I can stay calm.
try: If someone pushes back on a good choice of yours today, answer in one calm sentence and leave it there.

title: You bow to what your own hands carved?
subtitle: Worshipping something you made yourself
then: When they came to rebuke him, Ibrahim turned it back on them. Ibn Kathir says he meant: {trap}do you worship idols which you yourselves carve and fashion with your own hands?{/trap}
now: You built the career, the image, the house, the follower count. Now you check it, fear for it, and give up sleep for it. {trap}Your own work has become your master.{/trap} {idea}Things you made should serve you, while you serve Allah.{/idea}
old: What I built is mine to protect at any cost.
new: What I make should never become what I bow to.
try: Name one thing you built that now controls you. Set one limit on it today.

title: Allah made you, and also what you make.
subtitle: Even your work is His creation
then: Ibn Kathir says this may mean Allah created you and what you do, or you and what you make, and {idea}both views are synonymous{/idea}. The carvers and their carvings are both created. So how can one be worshipped?
now: The app you coded, the cake you baked, the report your boss praised. {idea}The skill, the hands, the idea, the materials: all made by Allah.{/idea} That does not shrink your effort. It gives it a place to bow.
old: What I make comes from me alone.
new: My skill and my work are both created by Allah. That is a reason to thank Him.
try: After you finish one piece of work today, say alhamdulillah and mean it.

title: When they lost the argument, they built a fire.
subtitle: Force is what is left when proof is gone
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}when the proof had been established against them, they resolved to seize him by force{/trap}. They said: build him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire. Allah saved him, as told in Surat Al-Anbiya'.
now: You are losing an argument with your spouse, your sibling, your coworker. You feel the urge to get louder, to threaten, to bring up old wounds. {trap}That is the fire-building move.{/trap} {idea}The braver move is to admit they might be right.{/idea}
old: When I am losing, I need to push harder.
new: When I have no answer, the honest thing is to listen, not to get louder.
try: The next time you lose a point in a disagreement today, say: you have a fair point.

title: They planned against him, and ended up the lowest.
subtitle: The plot turned upside down
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah saved him from the fire and caused him to prevail over them{/reward}, making his proof supreme. The people who planned to destroy him became the lowest.
now: Someone at work is building a case against you. A relative is spreading a story. You lie awake running through every move they could make. {idea}They have plans. Allah has the final one.{/idea} Keep doing right.
old: If people are plotting against me, I must out-plot them.
new: I do what is right and leave the plotters to Allah. He has the last move.
try: Tonight, name the situation in a short du'a and hand it over. Then sleep.

title: I am going to my Lord. He will guide me.
subtitle: Leaving with no map but trust
then: Ibn Kathir says after Allah helped Ibrahim against his people, and {trap}after he gave up hoping they would ever believe{/trap}, he emigrated away from them. He did not name a city. He named his Lord.
now: You are leaving a job that compromised your faith, moving away from a crowd that was dragging you down. You do not know what is next. {idea}Ibrahim did not either.{/idea} He just knew Who he was going to.
old: I cannot leave until I know exactly where I am going.
new: If I am leaving for Allah's sake, I can trust Him to show me the way.
try: If you are facing a change for Allah's sake, say his words today: I am going to my Lord, He will guide me.

title: Alone in a new land, he asked for righteous family.
subtitle: A prayer to replace what he left behind
then: Ibn Kathir explains Ibrahim asked for {reward}obedient children, in compensation for his people and relatives whom he had left{/reward}. He had given up his family for Allah, and he asked Allah for a new one.
now: You moved away for work and the family group chat feels far. Or you are hoping to marry, or to have a child. {idea}Ask Allah not just for people, but for righteous ones.{/idea} That is what Ibrahim asked for.
old: I just want a family. Character can come later.
new: When I ask for family, I ask for righteousness first.
try: Add this short du'a to your prayer today: my Lord, grant me from the righteous.

title: The good news of a forbearing boy.
subtitle: Isma'il, named by his character before his trial

row.title: forbearing
sub: the trait the test will need

then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}this child was Isma'il{/reward}, the first son whose birth was announced to Ibrahim, older than Ishaq. He notes Ibrahim was eighty-six when Isma'il was born. The boy is described as forbearing before anything else happens.
now: Think of the people you love. What is the one quality you would thank Allah for in each of them? {idea}Character is a gift, not just a skill.{/idea} The patience in a child is a blessing to name and nurture.
old: Children are a blessing because of what they achieve.
new: A child's gentle, patient character is itself the good news.
try: Tell a child or young person in your life one good quality you see in them today.

title: A father asks his son what he thinks.
subtitle: The hardest command, met with a conversation

row.title: Ibrahim
sub: so look, what do you think?

then: 'Ubayd bin 'Umayr said {idea}the dreams of the Prophets are revelation{/idea}, so this was a command from Allah to a Prophet. Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim told his son to make it easier for him and to test his patience. The young man answered: if Allah wills, you will find me patient.
now: This was a unique test for a Prophet, not a pattern for anyone. But notice how he did it. A hard family decision, a move abroad, a sickness. {idea}He did not hide it. He asked: what do you think?{/idea}
old: Hard decisions are for me to make alone and announce.
new: Even the hardest news is easier to carry when shared with honest conversation.
try: In one family decision this week, ask the person most affected: what do you think?

title: Both of them submitted. That was the real moment.
subtitle: When surrender is complete on both sides
then: Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and others said {idea}they submitted and followed the command of Allah{/idea}: Ibrahim obeyed Allah, and Isma'il obeyed Allah and his father. Ibn Kathir says he laid him face down so he would not have to see his face.
now: There is a moment when you stop arguing with Allah's decree. After the diagnosis. After the job is gone. {idea}The heart says yes, even before you know how it ends.{/idea} That yes is what the test was looking for.
old: Submitting means I have no feelings about it.
new: Submitting is choosing Allah's way with my heart, even while it is hard.
try: Name one thing you are still arguing with Allah about. Say quietly: I accept, help me through it.

title: At the very edge, a voice called his name.
subtitle: O Ibrahim: relief that arrives at the last moment
then: In the report from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibrahim had laid his son down and {reward}then he was called from behind{/reward}. He turned and saw a fine, horned, white ram. The call came exactly when the obedience was complete.
now: You have been praying for months. The rent is due tomorrow. The results come in an hour. {idea}Help often comes at the edge, not before it.{/idea} Allah knows your name and your moment.
old: If help has not come yet, it is not coming.
new: Allah's relief can arrive at the last moment, and it is never late.
try: If you are waiting on something hard today, keep doing your part and say: Allah knows my moment.

title: You have fulfilled the vision. This is how Allah rewards.
subtitle: Obedience in hard things opens a way out

row.title: a way out
sub: for those who obey in hard things

then: Ibn Kathir says the purpose of the dream was {idea}fulfilled by his laying down his son{/idea}. Then: this is how We deal with those who obey Us in difficult things; {reward}We make for them a way out{/reward}. He links it to 65:2-3.
now: You turned down the haram money, and now the bills are tight. You kept your word when it cost you. {idea}Allah sees the willingness, not just the result.{/idea} And He promises a way out for that kind of person.
old: If I obey Allah in this, I will only lose.
new: When I obey Allah in something hard, He opens a way I could not see.
try: Do one hard right thing today that you have been avoiding. Trust the way out.

title: This was a clear test, and he passed it.
subtitle: A trial measured by how quickly he obeyed

row.title: a clear trial
sub: showing what is in the heart

then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}it was clearly a test{/idea} when he was commanded to sacrifice his son, and he hastened to do it in submission and obedience. He links it to 53:37: Ibrahim who fulfilled all that was asked.
now: A loss, a hard boss, a long wait for a child. It is easy to feel targeted. {idea}The verse names it a trial: something that shows what you are made of.{/idea} Tests are where faith becomes visible.
old: This hardship means Allah is displeased with me.
new: A hard test can be the place where my faith is shown and honored.
try: Name your current test in one sentence. Ask Allah to help you pass it well.

title: Allah ransomed the son with a great sacrifice.
subtitle: What was offered was returned, with a ram in its place
then: Ibn Kathir reports the ransom was a ram, and Ibn 'Abbas said {reward}a ram which had grazed in Paradise{/reward}. A report says its horns were kept in the Ka'bah until it burned. Ibn Kathir also notes the purpose of the command was to reward Ibrahim's patience and resolve.
now: Sometimes you hand something over to Allah, a plan, a relationship, a dream job, expecting to lose it. {idea}And it comes back to you, or something better is put in its place.{/idea} What He asks for is the heart.
old: If I give this up for Allah, it is gone forever.
new: What I truly hand to Allah is never lost. He knows what to return and what to replace.
