try: Think of one thing you are gripping tightly. Tell Allah today it is His to keep or return.

title: Like Nuh, Ibrahim was left a good name.
subtitle: The same honor given after the same kind of trial
then: The same words were said of Nuh in verse 78. Ibrahim lost his people and his homeland and was asked for his son. {reward}Allah left for him an honored name among those who came after.{/reward}
now: You may give up a lot for your faith: a friendship, a promotion, a place you loved. {idea}What you lose for Allah is not erased.{/idea} The verse repeats so you notice the pattern.
old: What I give up for Allah just disappears.
new: Allah turns what I give up for Him into something that lasts.
try: Remember one sacrifice you made for Allah. Thank Him for letting you make it.

title: Peace upon Ibrahim, the man thrown into fire.
subtitle: Peace given to the one who was given none by his people

picture.label: From his people, then from Allah

then: His own people built a fire for him. His father rejected him. {reward}Allah greets him with peace{/reward}, as He greeted Nuh. The surah sets this beside what his enemies wanted for him.
now: Some people in your life may never speak well of you. {idea}What Allah says about you outlasts every opinion.{/idea} His peace is the greeting worth living for.
old: I am defined by how people treat me.
new: Allah's word about me matters more than anything people say.
try: When someone hurts you today, say salam to them anyway, and ask Allah for His peace.

title: Thus We reward the good: a way out every time.
subtitle: The same promise, now proven by Ibrahim
then: This line was said after Nuh and again after Ibrahim's trial. Ibn Kathir explained it as {reward}this is how We deal with those who obey Us in things that are difficult for them; We make for them a way out.{/reward}
now: You read this and think: that was for Prophets. But the word is thus, a method. {idea}The same Lord who rescued Ibrahim sees your small act of good on a tired Tuesday.{/idea}
old: Allah's help like this was only for Prophets.
new: Allah's way of rewarding good is a pattern that includes me.
try: Do one good deed today and expect good from Allah because of it.

title: After everything, he is called simply: a believing servant.
subtitle: The Friend of Allah, summed up in one phrase
then: The same line closed Nuh's story in verse 81. Ibrahim broke idols, faced the fire, left home, and passed the hardest test. {idea}Allah sums it all up: he was one of Our believing servants.{/idea}
now: Your life will not have fire or idols in a town square. It will have a commute, a family, small temptations. {idea}The title is the same one, and it is open to you.{/idea}
old: Faith like Ibrahim's is out of my reach.
new: The core of his greatness is a title I can also work toward: believing servant.
try: Ask Allah today to write you among His believing servants.

title: After the test, more good news: Ishaq.
subtitle: A second son, a Prophet from the righteous
then: Ibn Kathir says that having given the news of Isma'il, Allah {reward}immediately follows that with the glad tidings of his brother Ishaq{/reward}. Muhammad bin Ka'b noted that Ishaq's own son was also promised, as in 11:71.
now: You gave up something for Allah and braced for emptiness. {reward}Then a new door opened{/reward}: a friend, a job, a peace you did not expect. {idea}Allah's gifts often come in pairs.{/idea}
old: Once I give something up, that is the end of the story.
new: After I give for Allah, He often adds more than I expected.
try: Write down one good thing that came to you after a loss. Thank Allah for it.

title: Blessed parents, but each descendant chooses their own way.
subtitle: A great family does not guarantee a good person
then: Allah blessed Ibrahim and Ishaq, then says plainly that among their descendants are {idea}those who do good{/idea} and {trap}those who clearly wrong themselves{/trap}. Ibn Kathir compares it to the blessing given to Nuh and those with him in 11:48.
now: Your grandfather was the imam. Your parents never missed a prayer. {trap}That is a blessing, not a pass.{/trap} {idea}Every person in a family still writes their own page.{/idea}
old: I come from a good family, so I am fine.
new: A good family is a gift. My own deeds are still mine to answer for.
try: Thank Allah for one good thing your family gave you, then do one deed of your own today.

title: Two brothers, one favor: prophethood for Musa and Harun.
subtitle: Allah's grace given to a team
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us {idea}how He blessed Musa and Harun with prophethood{/idea}. The surah moves on to the next pair of Prophets, two brothers who carried the message together.
now: Think of the sibling, cousin, or friend who stands with you in doing good. The one who wakes you for Fajr, who helps with the hard family conversation. {idea}That partnership is itself a favor from Allah.{/idea}
old: What I have in my faith I built myself.
new: Every good thing I carry, and every good partner I have, is a favor from Allah.
try: Message one person who helps you stay on the right path and thank them.

title: Saved from years of crushing oppression.
subtitle: Musa, Harun and their people rescued
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saved them and the believers from {trap}the oppression of Fir'awn and his people{/trap}, who persecuted them by killing their sons and forcing them into the most menial tasks. The phrase great distress was used for Nuh too.
now: Your distress might be a controlling boss, a debt that never shrinks, a home that does not feel safe. {idea}The same words that rescued Nuh rescued Musa's people.{/idea} Ask for that rescue and take the steps you can.
old: My situation is too big for anything to change.
new: Allah has rescued people from great distress before. He can do it again.
try: Name your distress to Allah in a du'a today, then take one small practical step out of it.

title: The oppressed became the ones who prevailed.
subtitle: Help from Allah turned the weak into victors
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}ultimately caused them to prevail{/reward} over those who oppressed them. The surah was heard by a small group of persecuted Muslims in Makkah, who could not imagine winning. It was meant for them.
now: You feel like the small one in the room: the junior at work, the new one in the class, the only one trying to stay clean. {idea}Victory belongs to those Allah helps, not those who look strong.{/idea}
old: Whoever looks strongest now will win.
new: The one Allah helps is the one who prevails, however weak they look.
try: Ask Allah for help today in the one area where you feel smallest.

title: Then they were given a Book that makes things clear.
subtitle: The Tawrah, after the rescue
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}revealed to Musa the Clear and Mighty Book, which is the Tawrah{/idea}, citing 21:48 where it is called the criterion and a shining light. Rescue came first, then a Book to live by.
now: You finally got the free time, the job security, the place of your own. {idea}Freedom is not the end goal. It is room to live by guidance.{/idea} Allah gave you a clear Book too.
old: Once my problems are solved, I can relax.
new: Relief is room to follow guidance, not a break from it.
try: Use part of your next free hour to read a page of the Quran with its meaning.

title: Guided to the straight path, in words and deeds.
subtitle: Guidance that shapes what you say and do
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the straight path Musa and Harun were guided to was {idea}with regard to words and deeds{/idea}. Having the Book was not enough. They were guided to live it.
now: You know the right thing. The test is the text you send, the price you charge, the way you talk to your mother. {idea}The straight path runs through your mouth and your hands.{/idea}
old: As long as my beliefs are right, I am on the path.
new: The straight path shows up in what I say and do, not only what I believe.
try: Pick one thing you say often that you know is not right. Replace it today.

title: Like Nuh and Ibrahim, they are spoken of with honor.
subtitle: The good name left for Musa and Harun

picture.label: The same gift, a third time

then: Ibn Kathir says this means {reward}after they died they would be mentioned in good terms and spoken of highly{/reward}. It is the third time the surah uses these words, each time after a Prophet was rescued.
now: Fir'awn had palaces and an army. Musa had a staff and a brother. Ask who is mentioned with honor today. {idea}The surah keeps repeating it so the lesson sticks.{/idea}
old: Power is what makes a name last.
new: Faithfulness, not power, is what Allah makes last.
try: Think of what you would want said about you after you are gone. Do one thing toward it today.

title: Peace upon Musa and Harun, together.
subtitle: Two brothers greeted in one breath
then: After the rescue, the help, the Book and the guidance, Allah greets {reward}both brothers together with peace{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this explains the good mention left for them.
now: Siblings fight over inheritance, drift apart over a wedding, stop calling. {idea}Musa and Harun are greeted with peace in one breath.{/idea} Brothers and sisters can carry good together.
old: My sibling and I are just too different to work together.
new: Siblings who stand together for good are honored together.
try: Call or message a brother or sister today, just to say salam.

title: This is how good is repaid.
subtitle: Musa and Harun, rescued and remembered

row.title: a pattern
sub: this is how Allah repays good

then: Musa and Harun lived under Fir'awn, who killed the sons of their people and forced them into the lowest work. Allah saved them, {reward}gave them the clear Scripture{/reward}, and left them a good name after they died. Then He says this is not a one-off: {idea}it is how He treats those who do good.{/idea}
now: You stay honest at a job where cutting corners is normal. You keep visiting a difficult parent when nobody notices. It feels like it goes nowhere. {idea}This verse says it is going somewhere.{/idea} Good is not lost in the system. It is repaid, by a Lord who keeps a pattern.
old: Doing good is nice, but it rarely changes how things turn out.
new: Good done for Allah sits inside a pattern of repayment He has promised to keep.
try: Do one quiet good thing today that nobody will thank you for, and leave the repayment to Allah.

title: Their highest title was servant who believes.
subtitle: What Allah chose to call two great prophets
then: After listing everything given to Musa and Harun, the rescue, the Book, the good name, the passage closes on one description. {idea}They were two of Our believing servants.{/idea} Not leaders, not victors. Servants. That was the root of all the rest.
now: Your LinkedIn headline. The title on your door. The way people introduce you at a wedding. You spend years building a name. {idea}The one name that lasts is servant of Allah who believes.{/idea} Everything else is a role you hold for a while.
old: I will matter once I have the right title.
new: The best thing that can be said of me is that I believed and served Allah.
try: Before your next task, say quietly: I am doing this as Allah's servant. Notice if it changes how you do it.

title: Ilyas was a messenger too.
subtitle: A less famous name in the same line

picture.label: The line of messengers so far

then: The surah moves through a line of prophets and now names Ilyas. Some early scholars said Ilyas is another name for Idris; others traced him to the line of Harun. {idea}What the verse makes certain is simpler: he was one of the messengers.{/idea}
now: Most of the people who keep a mosque, a family, or a hospital ward running are names nobody will put on a poster. {reward}Allah records them anyway.{/reward} A short mention in the Quran is still a mention by Allah.
old: If I am not well known, my work does not really count.
new: Allah names those He sent, whether people talk about them or not.
try: Thank one person today whose work keeps your life running and who rarely gets noticed.

title: His first words were a question, not an attack.
subtitle: Ilyas opens with: will you not fear Allah?
then: Ilyas was sent to his own people. Ibn Kathir explains the question as: {idea}do you not fear Allah when you worship others instead of Him?{/idea} He does not open with insults. He opens by asking them to look at what they are doing.
now: Your friend is drifting into something that is hurting them. You want to lecture. {idea}A real question often does more than a speech.{/idea} Do you feel at peace with this? Questions leave the door open for the other person to walk through.
old: To correct someone I have to tell them plainly how wrong they are.
new: An honest question about Allah can reach a heart that a lecture would close.
try: Next time you want to correct someone, try one gentle question instead of a statement.

title: Calling on a statue while leaving the Best of creators.
subtitle: The strange trade Ilyas pointed out

row.title: Ba'l
sub: an idol, the word means lord

then: Ba'l, early scholars said, means lord, and was the name of an idol. One report links it to the people of Baalbek, west of Damascus. Ilyas puts the two side by side: {trap}you call on a thing that was made{/trap}, and {idea}you leave the One who makes everything{/idea}.
now: At 2 a.m. you refresh the bank app, the job portal, the test results page, as if they could rescue you. {trap}You call on the screen.{/trap} The One who made you, the screen, and the people behind it is right there. {idea}Turn to Him first.{/idea}
old: I pray, but in a crisis I really rely on whatever seems to hold the power.
new: Everything I lean on was made. It makes no sense to leave its Maker for it.
try: When worry hits today, make a short dua before you check your phone.

title: Your Lord, and the Lord of your grandparents too.
subtitle: Allah is not new to their family

row.title: Allah came first
sub: Lord of the very first ancestors

then: Ilyas reminds his people that Allah is not a stranger to them. {idea}He is your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says this means He alone deserves worship, with no partner. The idol was the newcomer, not Allah.
now: Some family habits feel sacred only because they are old. The superstition at weddings. The way your family handles anger. {idea}Go back far enough and you find Allah was there first.{/idea} Returning to Him is not rebellion against your roots. It is the oldest root.
old: This is how my family has always done it, so it must be right.
new: Allah was my ancestors' Lord before any custom. Coming back to Him is going home.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly: does this come from Allah, or just from us?

title: They called him a liar, and they will be brought forward.
subtitle: Denial does not cancel the meeting

row.title: if I reject it, it goes away

then: His people did not argue the point. {trap}They simply denied him.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that they will be brought forth for the reckoning on the Day of Judgment. Saying no to a warning does not remove what it warns about.
now: You ignore the letter from the bank. You skip the check-up because you do not want to hear it. {trap}Not looking feels like safety.{/trap} But the appointment is still on the calendar. {idea}Better to face it now, while there is time to change.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about the reckoning, I do not have to deal with it.
new: The meeting with Allah is coming either way. Facing it now is the kind choice.
try: Think of one thing you have been avoiding that you know you will answer for. Take one small step on it today.

title: Except the servants Allah made sincere.
subtitle: The exception inside the warning
then: Right after the warning comes a door. Ibn Kathir says these chosen servants are {reward}those who believe in Allah alone{/reward}. Even in a people who denied, the warning was never meant to include the sincere.
now: Your whole office laughs about faith. Your group chat treats prayer as a joke. You can feel like you are carried along with them. {reward}You are not.{/reward} Allah sees the one person who stays sincere in the room.
old: If everyone around me is going one way, I am stuck going with them.
new: Allah always leaves an exception, and sincerity is how I stand inside it.
try: Do one act of worship today purely for Allah, without telling anyone.

title: His people rejected him. Later generations praised him.
subtitle: The name that outlived the rejection

row.title: Allah
sub: who left him a good name

then: The same words were said of Nuh, Ibrahim, and Musa and Harun. Now they come for Ilyas. Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}he is praised and spoken of highly{/reward} by those who came later. His own people rejected him. {idea}History did not.{/idea}
now: You are the one at work who will not fudge the numbers, and you get labeled difficult. You are the sibling who keeps the family honest, and it costs you. {reward}What people say now is not the final record.{/reward}
old: If people do not appreciate me now, my effort was wasted.
new: Allah can give a lasting good name to someone the people around them rejected.
try: Make a short dua for someone who stood for what was right and was not thanked for it.

title: Peace upon Ilyasin.
subtitle: Allah Himself sends him peace
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Ilyasin is another way of saying Ilyas, as Arabs said Isma'il and Isma'in, Mika'il and Mika'in. The point is the greeting itself. {reward}After a life of being denied, he is greeted with peace by Allah.{/reward}
now: You leave a job, a friendship, or a family meeting where nobody said goodbye properly. It stings for days. {reward}Imagine being greeted by Allah with peace.{/reward} That is the welcome worth working toward.
old: I need the people around me to see me off with kind words.
new: A greeting of peace from Allah outweighs every goodbye I did not get.
try: Greet one person today with a full salam, slowly, meaning it.

title: The same promise, now for a man his people refused.
subtitle: The refrain repeated for Ilyas
then: For Musa and Harun this line came after a visible victory over Fir'awn. For Ilyas it comes after {trap}his people denied him.{/trap} The reward is the same. {idea}Allah repays the good that was done, not the applause it got.{/idea}
now: You tutored a cousin and they still failed. You gave advice and it was ignored. You raised your kids carefully and one of them drifted. {idea}Your good was still good.{/idea} Allah does not grade you on other people's choices.
old: If my effort did not change anyone, it did not count.
new: Allah rewards the good I did, even when the result was out of my hands.
try: Think of one effort that seemed to fail. Ask Allah to accept it, and let the result go.

title: Whatever else he was, he was a believing servant.
subtitle: The closing line on Ilyas
then: The story of Ilyas ends the same way the story of Musa and Harun did. {idea}He was one of Our believing servants.{/idea} His people's verdict on him is not recorded as the last word. Allah's is.
now: One day someone will sum you up. A eulogy, a family story, a line in a group chat. {idea}What will Allah's summary be?{/idea} That is the only one that lasts, and you are still writing it today.
old: I will be remembered for what I achieved.
new: The summary that counts is whether Allah calls me His believing servant.
try: Write one sentence you hope would be true of you before Allah. Keep it where you will see it.

title: Lut was one of the messengers.
subtitle: A messenger sent to a people who refused him
then: After Ilyas, the surah turns to Lut. Ibn Kathir says Allah sent His servant and messenger Lut to his people, {trap}and they denied him.{/trap} {idea}His rank came from being sent, not from being believed.{/idea}
now: You are the only one in your friend group who will not join in. You are the parent saying no when every other parent says yes. {idea}Standing for what is right does not need a majority.{/idea} Lut stood almost alone and Allah still called him one of the messengers.
old: If nobody listens to me, maybe I am the one who is wrong.
new: Being right with Allah does not depend on how many people agree.
try: Hold one small line today that you know is right, even if you are the only one holding it.

title: Allah saved him and his family, all of them.
subtitle: Rescue for those who stood with him

row.title: saved
sub: from among a people who denied

row.title: a whole town is lost
sub: so everyone in it is lost

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saved Lut from among his people, {reward}him and his family{/reward}. Surrounded by a whole town that rejected him, he was not swept away with them. {idea}Allah knew exactly who stood with His messenger.{/idea}
now: You work at a company in trouble, live in a neighborhood going downhill, belong to a family with a bad name. {reward}Allah does not see you as a crowd.{/reward} He sees you, one person, and what you chose.
old: I will go down with whatever group I belong to.
new: Allah deals with me as a person, and He rescues those who hold on to Him.
try: Make dua today for your own household by name, one person at a time.

title: Except an old woman who stayed behind.
subtitle: Living with a prophet did not save his wife
then: Ibn Kathir says the old woman was Lut's wife, {trap}who was destroyed along with her people.{/trap} She shared a home with a messenger. {idea}She shared her heart with those who denied him.{/idea}
now: Your father prays at the front of the mosque. Your spouse is the religious one. You are in the WhatsApp group with all the good people. {idea}None of that is your faith.{/idea} Living near goodness is not the same as choosing it.
old: My family is religious, so I am covered.
new: Nobody's closeness to Allah can stand in for my own.
try: Do one act of worship today that is yours alone, not one you do because your family does it.

title: Then the rest were destroyed.
subtitle: The end of a people who refused
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah destroyed them with different kinds of punishment and turned their land into a foul lake. {trap}They had been warned, and they denied.{/trap} The story is told to the people of Makkah, {idea}who were mocking the same kind of warning.{/idea}
now: A bad habit you keep saying you will fix next month. A wrong you keep meaning to set right. {trap}Each day without consequence feels like proof it does not matter.{/trap} {idea}It is actually time being given to you.{/idea}
old: Nothing bad has come from this yet, so it must be fine.
new: The time before consequences is a mercy to use, not a sign that none are coming.
try: Name one habit you keep postponing. Do the smallest first step to change it today.

title: You drive past their ruins every morning.
subtitle: The lesson was on the trade route

row.title: a sign
sub: left there for them to read

then: Ibn Kathir explains the site was on a well-travelled route, the highway between Arabia and Syria, close to the Dead Sea. {idea}The people of Makkah passed it on their trade journeys.{/idea} The lesson was not hidden. {trap}It was on their commute.{/trap}
now: The hospital you drive past. The cemetery on the way to work. The friend's empty chair at the family dinner. {idea}Reminders are already in your route.{/idea} You only have to stop treating them as background.
old: I would reflect more if I came across something that made me think.
new: Allah has already put signs on my daily path. I just pass them without reading.
try: On your next commute, notice one thing that reminds you of death or of Allah. Pause on it for a breath.

title: And at night. Will you not think?
subtitle: Morning and evening, the same unread lesson

row.title: thinking
sub: learning that a like end awaits

then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: {idea}will you not learn a lesson from them{/idea} and realize that a similar end awaits those who deny? They saw the place day and night. {trap}They never connected it to themselves.{/trap}
now: You scroll past news of a sudden death at breakfast and again before bed. You say how sad, and keep scrolling. {idea}The verse asks you to stop and think.{/idea} What does this mean for how I live tomorrow?
old: I know life is short. I hear about death all the time.
new: Hearing about it is not the same as letting it change how I live.
try: Tonight, before sleep, ask yourself one question: if today were my last, what would I wish I had done?

title: Yunus was one of the messengers.
subtitle: A prophet whose story includes a slip

picture.label: The last story in the line

then: The surah now tells the story of Yunus. Ibn Kathir quotes the Prophet ﷺ in the Two Sahihs: {idea}it is not right for anyone to say I am better than Yunus bin Matta.{/idea} His story includes a slip, and {trap}the slip does not make him smaller.{/trap}
now: Someone you look up to messes up in public. A teacher, an imam, a parent. {trap}It is tempting to feel taller.{/trap} {idea}Their slip is not your rise.{/idea} The story of Yunus asks you to learn from it, not look down from it.
old: When a good person falls, it shows I am not so bad after all.
new: Someone else's mistake is a lesson for me, never a reason to rank myself above them.
try: Next time you hear of someone's failure, make a quiet dua for them instead of commenting.

title: He ran off to a ship already full.
subtitle: Leaving his post, onto a loaded boat

row.title: Allah is on every ship
sub: there is no away from Him

then: The verse says Yunus ran away, and the story calls what he did {idea}an act worthy of blame.{/idea} He boarded a ship that, as Ibn Abbas said, {trap}was filled with cargo.{/trap} A full ship, a storm coming, and a prophet away from his people.
now: The project gets hard, so you start updating your CV. The marriage gets tense, so you stay late at the office. The duty feels heavy, so you book a trip. {idea}Sometimes the hard place is exactly where Allah wants you.{/idea}
old: When things get too hard, the answer is to get out.
new: Before I run, I should ask whether Allah has released me from where I am.
try: Think of one place you want to escape from. Make dua for guidance before deciding anything.

title: They drew lots, and he lost.
subtitle: The storm, the overloaded ship, the draw
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the ship was being pounded by waves and at risk of sinking. {trap}They drew lots to choose who would go overboard.{/trap} Yunus lost the draw three times. The sailors did not want to throw him, but {idea}the decree kept pointing at him.{/idea}
now: You miss the train, lose the job offer, get the one test result you dreaded. {trap}It feels like the draw is rigged against you.{/trap} {idea}It may be Allah turning you back toward something.{/idea} Losing a draw can be the start of a return.
old: Things keep going wrong for me. I must just be unlucky.
new: When doors keep closing, Allah may be steering me somewhere I need to go.
try: Look at one recent setback and ask: what might Allah be turning me toward?

title: Swallowed by the fish, knowing he was at fault.
subtitle: The lowest point of the story

row.title: it is the end of me

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah commanded a great fish to swallow Yunus {idea}without cutting his flesh or breaking his bones.{/idea} The verse says he was blameworthy, {trap}he had done something deserving of blame.{/trap} Even inside the punishment, he was being kept safe.
now: You know the mess you are in is your own doing. The debt, the argument, the lie that grew. {trap}The weight of knowing it was you is the heaviest part.{/trap} {idea}Owning it is not the end. It is where the way out begins.{/idea}
old: I caused this, so I do not deserve a way out.
new: Admitting I am at fault is the first step out, and Allah can protect me even inside my mistake.
try: Say to Allah, in your own words, one thing you know you got wrong. Nothing more.

title: His glorification of Allah was his rope out.
subtitle: What he did in the good days saved him

row.title: I will pray when I need it
know Allah in ease
sub: He will know you in hardship

then: Scholars gave two meanings. Many, including Ibn Jarir, said it was {reward}the good he had done in times of ease.{/reward} Ibn Kathir quotes the hadith: remember Allah in ease and He will remember you in hardship. Others said it was his cry in the darkness: {idea}none has the right to be worshipped but You, glory be to You, I was a wrongdoer.{/idea}
now: Life is calm right now. Salary in, kids healthy, no hospital visits. {reward}This is the time to build the habit.{/reward} The dhikr you say on an easy Tuesday is the rope you will hold on a terrible Friday.
old: Things are fine at the moment, so I can relax my worship a bit.
new: The worship I do in easy times is what carries me when hard times arrive.
try: Pick one short dhikr and say it ten times today while things are calm.

title: Without it, the fish would have been his grave.
subtitle: How close the other ending was
then: The verse shows the other ending. {trap}He would have stayed in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection.{/trap} Ibn Kathir quotes a report that the angels recognized his weak voice from a far place, because {reward}his good deeds used to keep rising to them.{/reward}
now: You are in a place with no exits you can see. The diagnosis, the debt, the court date. {trap}Every human door is shut.{/trap} {idea}One door does not need a key you hold. It opens from the other side when you call.{/idea}
old: If I cannot find a way out myself, there is no way out.
new: When every door I can reach is shut, calling on Allah is still a door.
try: In your hardest situation right now, say the words of Yunus once, slowly: La ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.

title: Thrown onto a bare shore, weak and sick.
subtitle: Rescued, but not yet restored
then: Ibn Abbas and others said the shore was {trap}land with no vegetation and no buildings.{/trap} Yunus came out weak of body. {reward}He was saved{/reward}, but the recovery had not yet begun.
now: You got out of the bad job, the toxic relationship, the hospital bed. {trap}You expected to feel amazing. Instead you feel empty and tired.{/trap} {idea}That is still rescue.{/idea} Lying on the bare shore is part of being saved.
old: If Allah really answered me, I would feel better by now.
new: Being brought out is the first answer. Healing can come after, slowly.
try: If you are recovering from something, give yourself one hour of rest today without guilt.

title: Allah grew a gourd vine over him.
subtitle: Shade and food on an empty shore

row.title: a simple plant
sub: exactly what a sick man needs

then: Many early scholars said the plant was squash. Ibn Kathir lists its benefits: {reward}it grows fast, its broad leaves give shade, flies avoid it, and its fruit nourishes.{/reward} {idea}Allah's care came as an ordinary plant, perfectly suited to a weak man on a bare shore.{/idea}
now: After the hard season, help arrives small. A neighbor brings soup. A coworker covers your shift. A friend sends a voice note at the right moment. {idea}That is the gourd vine.{/idea} Do not overlook it because it looks ordinary.
old: I am waiting for Allah to fix this in a big way.
new: Allah often sends care through small, ordinary things that fit my need exactly.
try: Notice one small kindness someone shows you today, and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Sent back to a hundred thousand, or more.
subtitle: After the fish, the mission resumes
then: Ibn Kathir says it is as if Yunus was commanded, after coming out of the fish, {idea}to go back to the people he had first been sent to.{/idea} His slip did not end his mission. {reward}He was sent again, to a great number of people.{/reward}
now: You let your team down, broke a promise to your kids, fell back into the old habit. {trap}You assume you are finished.{/trap} {idea}Allah sent Yunus back to the very work he left.{/idea} Repentance often means returning to the place you walked away from.
old: After what I did, I have no right to go back to that role.
new: After sincere repentance, Allah can send me back to the very work I ran from.
try: Return to one duty you dropped. Do just the first small piece of it today.

title: They all believed, and were given life for a while.
subtitle: The one town whose faith saved it
then: Ibn Kathir says the people Yunus was sent to {reward}all believed in him{/reward}, and Allah let them enjoy life until their appointed end. He links it to the verse naming them as {idea}the one town whose faith, when it came, benefited them.{/idea}
now: After the stories of destroyed towns, this one ends well. A whole people turned around. {idea}It is never too late while you are still breathing.{/idea} Your family, your street, your own heart can change direction.
old: Some people are too far gone to change.
new: A whole people turned back to Allah and were spared. Change is possible.
try: Make dua today for one person you have given up on, that Allah turns their heart.

title: Daughters for Him, sons for themselves?
subtitle: A share they would never choose for themselves
then: The idolaters of Makkah said the angels were daughters of Allah. Ibn Kathir notes that when one of them was told of a baby girl, {trap}his face would darken with grief.{/trap} Yet they gave Allah the very share they disliked. {idea}Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to question them on it.{/idea}
now: The family that cheers louder for a baby boy. The relative who says better luck next time when a girl is born. {trap}The old attitude did not fully die.{/trap} {idea}Notice if any of it lives in your own words.{/idea} A daughter is a gift from the same Lord.
old: Preferring sons is just a cultural thing, it does not mean anything.
new: The Quran calls out this attitude directly. A daughter is not a lesser blessing.
try: Say something warm and specific today to a daughter, sister, or niece about who she is.

title: Were they there when the angels were created?
subtitle: Confident claims about what they never saw
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}how did they decide the angels are female when they did not witness their creation?{/idea} He links it to another verse that says {trap}their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.{/trap}
now: You forward a message about the unseen with total confidence. You state what Allah is thinking about someone. {trap}You were not there.{/trap} {idea}Speaking about the unseen without knowledge is a serious thing.{/idea} I do not know is often the honest answer.
old: Everyone says it, so it must be true.
new: If I did not see it and Allah did not reveal it, I should not claim it.
try: Before you share the next religious claim you see online, check where it comes from.

title: It comes from their own invented lie.
subtitle: Where the claim really came from
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}part of the lies they tell.{/trap} The verse opens with: no doubt. {idea}Their talk about Allah did not come from any revelation. It came from their own invention.{/idea}
now: A rumor starts in the family chat. Someone adds a detail. A month later everyone believes it. {trap}Invented things harden into facts when they are repeated.{/trap} {idea}Ask where a belief started before you build on it.{/idea}
old: If something has been said for long enough, it is probably true.
new: A lie repeated for generations is still a lie. Its source decides its worth.
try: Pick one thing you believe about Allah and ask yourself honestly: where did I learn this?

title: Allah has begotten, they said. They are liars.
subtitle: The claim, and the verdict on it
then: Ibn Kathir lists three things they said: {trap}that the angels were Allah's daughters, that Allah had offspring, and then they worshipped them.{/trap} Any one of these alone was enough to condemn them. {idea}Allah calls it plainly what it is: a lie.{/idea}
now: You hear someone describe Allah as if He needs something, a helper, a family, a favor. {idea}Allah is not like His creation.{/idea} Keeping His oneness clear in your own head is part of protecting your faith.
old: How people describe Allah is just a matter of opinion.
new: Saying Allah has a child is not a small opinion. Allah Himself calls it a lie.
try: Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas slowly today, thinking about each line.

title: Would He choose daughters over sons?
subtitle: Their own logic turned back on them
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}what would make Him choose daughters rather than sons?{/idea} By their own values, they had given Allah the lesser share. He links it to another verse that calls this {trap}an awful saying.{/trap}
now: You hold a belief that falls apart the moment someone asks you one honest question. {idea}That is not a reason to get defensive.{/idea} It is a gift. A belief that cannot survive a question was not worth holding.
old: If someone questions my belief, I should defend it no matter what.
new: A good question can show me where my thinking does not hold together.
try: Ask someone you trust one question about your faith you have never asked out loud.

title: What is wrong with you? How do you judge?
subtitle: A question about how they think
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question as {idea}what kind of reasoning makes you say that?{/idea} The idolaters were not following evidence. {trap}They were following what they liked and calling it judgment.{/trap}
now: You decide the coworker is lazy before you know what is happening at home. You decide a ruling is unfair because it is inconvenient. {trap}Preference dressed up as judgment.{/trap} {idea}Ask yourself: how did I really decide this?{/idea}
old: My conclusions come from thinking clearly.
new: I should check whether my judgment is reasoning or just what I want to be true.
try: Pick one strong opinion you formed this week and trace honestly how you reached it.

title: Will you not remember?
subtitle: The truth they already had inside them
then: After asking how they judge, Allah asks: {idea}will you not then remember?{/idea} The question is not asking them to learn something new. {trap}It asks why they forgot what was plain.{/trap}
now: You do not need another lecture to know that the late-night scroll is hurting you, or that you owe your mother a call. {idea}You already know.{/idea} Reminding is often just letting what you know reach the front of your mind.
old: I would change if I just knew more.
new: Often I already know enough. What I need is to remember it.
try: Write down one thing you already know you should do, and do it before the day ends.

title: Or do you have clear proof?
subtitle: Allah asks them for evidence

key.label: What a claim about Allah needs

then: Ibn Kathir explains the authority as {idea}evidence to prove what you say.{/idea} Allah does not simply silence them. He invites them to bring proof. {trap}They had none.{/trap}
now: Someone in the family insists on a rule about religion that sounds strange. You ask where it comes from. They get angry. {idea}Asking for proof is not disrespect.{/idea} The Quran itself asks for it.
old: Questioning what people say about religion is rude.
new: Asking for evidence is a Quranic habit, done with good manners.
try: Next time you hear a religious claim, gently ask: where is that from?

title: Then bring your book, if you are truthful.
subtitle: Show the scripture that says it
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}produce evidence from a Book revealed by Allah{/idea} that proves He has taken offspring. {trap}What you say is totally irrational.{/trap} Claims about Allah need words from Allah.
now: You hear things like Allah will not forgive you, or Allah wants you to suffer, from a voice in your own head. {idea}Bring the book.{/idea} Check those voices against what Allah actually said. Most of them have no source.
old: The harsh things I believe about how Allah sees me must be true.
new: What I believe about Allah should come from what He revealed, not from fear or habit.
try: Look up one verse today about Allah's mercy and read it slowly.

title: They invented a family tie between Allah and the jinn.
subtitle: And the jinn know they will be brought forth

row.title: the jinn are kin to Allah

then: Mujahid reported that when the idolaters said the angels were Allah's daughters, Abu Bakr asked who their mothers were. {trap}They said the daughters of the leaders of the jinn.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that those who say this {idea}will be brought forth on the Day of Reckoning{/idea} for speaking without knowledge.
now: One false claim needs a second to hold it up, then a third. The excuse at work turns into a story, then a whole cover. {trap}Lies need family trees.{/trap} {idea}The truth does not.{/idea}
old: One small untruth will not grow into anything.
new: A lie keeps needing new lies to support it. The truth stands on its own.
try: If you have told a small untruth recently, correct it today, simply and quietly.

title: Allah is far above what they describe.
subtitle: Subhan Allah after a list of false claims
then: After all the questions comes this. Ibn Kathir explains it as: {idea}exalted, sanctified and glorified be He far above having any offspring{/idea} and above everything the wrongdoers attribute to Him.
now: You read a comment that mocks Allah. You hear a careless joke about Him at a dinner. {idea}Subhan Allah is the right first response.{/idea} It is not running from the argument. It is putting Allah back where He belongs in your own heart.
old: When people say wrong things about Allah, I have to win the argument.
new: First I declare Allah above it in my heart, then I speak only if it helps.
try: When you hear something wrong about Allah today, say Subhan Allah quietly before anything else.

title: Except His chosen servants, who describe Him rightly.
subtitle: Those who follow what the prophets brought
then: Ibn Kathir says the people who describe Allah falsely are all of mankind, {reward}except those whom He chooses{/reward}: {idea}the ones who follow the truth revealed to every prophet.{/idea}
now: You picture Allah as a strict boss, or as someone who does not really notice. {trap}Both come from your imagination.{/trap} {reward}The chosen servants describe Him the way He described Himself.{/reward} That is a picture you can trust.
old: My image of Allah is shaped by how people have treated me.
new: I want to know Allah the way He described Himself, through His prophets.
try: Read one of Allah's names today and its meaning. Let it correct your picture of Him.

title: You, and whatever you worship.
subtitle: The idolaters and their idols addressed together
then: Allah now speaks directly to the idolaters. Ibn Kathir explains the address as {trap}you and those whom you worship{/trap} together. {idea}The sentence is left open here, and the next verse finishes it.{/idea}
now: The influencer and the lifestyle they sell. The crowd and the trend it worships. {trap}Together they look unstoppable.{/trap} {idea}Wait for how Allah finishes the sentence.{/idea}
old: Those who push false things together have a lot of power over me.
new: Whatever people gather around besides Allah, together they still cannot own my heart.
try: Notice one trend you feel pulled by today. Name it, and remind yourself it has no power over your choice.

title: You cannot lure anyone away from Him.
subtitle: False worship has no hold on a turned heart

row.title: Allah
sub: no one tempts away from Him

then: The small band of believers in Makkah was under heavy pressure, and the idolaters seemed to hold every advantage. Allah tells them: {idea}you cannot tempt anyone away from Him.{/idea} {trap}Their mockery and power{/trap} could not reach a heart that belonged to Allah.
now: You worry about your teenager, your new-Muslim friend, yourself. {trap}The world is loud and very persuasive.{/trap} {idea}It is not stronger than Allah's hold on a heart that turns to Him.{/idea}
old: With so much pressure around, keeping faith is a losing battle.
new: No one can pull a heart from Allah if it keeps turning to Him.
try: Make a short dua today asking Allah to keep your heart firm on faith.

title: Only those already heading for the Fire follow them.
subtitle: Who false worship actually reaches

key.label: What makes someone open to it

then: Ibn Kathir explains that the only ones who follow such false worship are {trap}those more misguided than its callers.{/trap} He links them to the verse about people who {idea}have hearts they do not understand with, eyes they do not see with, and ears they do not hear with.{/idea}
now: What makes you easy to pull is not how clever the pull is. {trap}It is how heedless you are when it comes.{/trap} The tired, distracted, half-awake heart. {idea}Keep your heart awake and the pull loses its grip.{/idea}
old: People fall for falsehood because it is so convincing.
new: Falsehood wins most easily over a heart that has stopped paying attention.
try: Take two minutes today with your phone away, and simply pay attention to your heart.

title: Every angel has a known place.
subtitle: The angels speak about themselves
then: Against the claim that angels are Allah's daughters, the angels speak. Ibn Kathir says {idea}each has his own place in the heavens which he does not overstep.{/idea} He quotes the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}there is no place in the lowest heaven without an angel standing or prostrating in it.{/reward}
now: You keep comparing your place to everyone else's. Their job, their house, their marriage. {idea}The angels know their place and fill it with worship.{/idea} Your place today is where Allah put you. Fill it well.
old: I would worship better if I were in a different situation.
new: Like the angels, I can serve Allah fully in exactly the place He has given me.
try: Do your main task today with full attention, as worship, right where you are.

title: We are the ones who stand in rows.
subtitle: The angels' rows, and ours in prayer
then: The surah opened by swearing by those ranged in rows. Ibn Kathir reports that Umar would turn to the people before prayer and say: {idea}make your rows straight, for Allah wants you to follow the ways of the angels.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}our rows have been made like the rows of the angels.{/reward}
now: Friday prayer. You are on your phone until the last second, then drift into a gap with half a step between you and the next person. {idea}Your row mirrors the angels' rows.{/idea} Close the gap, stand straight, and mean it.
old: How the rows look in prayer is just a detail.
new: Standing in a straight row, I am joining something the angels do in the heavens.
try: At your next prayer in congregation, close the gap and straighten your row on purpose.

title: We are the ones who glorify Him.
subtitle: Servants, not partners
then: Ibn Kathir explains the angels' words: {idea}we stand in rows and glorify the Lord{/idea}, declaring Him above any fault. {reward}We are His servants and in need of Him, humbling ourselves before Him.{/reward} The beings the idolaters worshipped are themselves worshippers.
now: You put someone on a pedestal: a scholar, a parent, a public figure. {idea}The best of creation glorify Allah and call themselves His servants.{/idea} Respect people, but keep worship for the One they worship.
old: Some people are so holy they are almost beyond being servants.
new: Even the angels say: we are servants who glorify Him. So is everyone I admire.
try: Say Subhan Allah thirty-three times after one prayer today.

title: They used to say something, before he came.
subtitle: What Quraysh said before the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir explains that before the Prophet ﷺ came, Quraysh {trap}used to wish{/trap} for someone to remind them about Allah. This verse opens the quote. {idea}The next two verses tell us what they said.{/idea}
now: If I ever had time, I would read Quran every day. If I lived near a mosque, I would pray there. {trap}We all have used-to-say sentences.{/trap} {idea}The test is what happens when the chance arrives.{/idea}
old: I would do better if the right conditions came.
new: When the chance I wished for arrives, my answer is what counts, not my old wish.
try: Think of one thing you said you would do if you could. If you now can, start it today.

title: If only we had a reminder like the people of old.
subtitle: They wished for a book of their own
then: Ibn Kathir says Quraysh used to wish for {reward}someone to remind them about Allah and bring them the Book of Allah.{/reward} He links it to the verse where they swore that if a warner came, {trap}they would be more guided than any nation.{/trap}
now: If I had grown up in a practicing family. If I could study with a real scholar. {trap}It always feels like the missing piece is outside you.{/trap} {idea}You have the Quran on your phone right now.{/idea}
old: I would be a better Muslim if I had better guidance around me.
new: The reminder is already in my hands. What I need is to open it.
try: Open the Quran today and read just one page with its meaning.

title: We would have been Allah's sincere servants.
subtitle: The promise they made about themselves
then: Ibn Kathir quotes the verse: they swore that if a warner came {reward}they would be more guided than any nation{/reward}, yet when one came {trap}it increased them only in flight from the truth.{/trap} Their promise about themselves did not survive the test.
now: You say, if I ever got rich, I would give so much. If I ever had kids, I would be so patient. {trap}Then the money comes. The kids come.{/trap} {idea}The person you promised to be is waiting to see if you show up.{/idea}
old: I know the kind of person I would be, given the chance.
new: My promises about my future self mean little until I keep them in the present.
try: Keep one small promise today that you made to yourself or to Allah.

title: Then it came, and they rejected it. They will know.
subtitle: The wish granted, and turned down
then: What they asked for arrived. {trap}They disbelieved in it.{/trap} Ibn Kathir calls the ending {idea}a definite and stern threat{/idea} because of their disbelief in their Lord and their rejection of His Messenger ﷺ.
now: You prayed for a job, and when it came you complained about it. You asked Allah for a sign, and when a reminder came you scrolled past. {idea}Sometimes the answer arrives, and the real test is whether you accept it.{/idea}
old: If Allah gave me what I asked for, I would surely be grateful.
new: When what I asked for arrives, I need to recognize and accept it, not wish for something else.
try: Name one prayer of yours that Allah has already answered. Thank Him for it today.

title: Allah's word for His messengers was given long ago.
subtitle: A promise already decided
then: This was revealed when {trap}most believers had already emigrated and only a small group remained with the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah{/trap}, facing persecution. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}it was stated in the first decree that the messengers and their followers will prevail{/idea}, in this world and the next.
now: You are in the middle of it: the long job search, the illness, the family that does not understand your faith. {trap}From inside, it looks like losing.{/trap} {reward}Allah's word about those who stay with Him was given long before your hard chapter.{/reward}
old: Right now it looks like I am losing, so I probably am.
new: How things look in the middle is not the end Allah has already written.
try: Write down one hard thing you are going through, and under it write: Allah's word came first.

title: They are the ones who will be helped to victory.
subtitle: The content of the promise

row.title: given victory
sub: in this world and the next

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah had already stated {reward}the messengers would prevail over the people who disbelieved in them{/reward}, and that He destroyed the disbelievers and saved His believing servants. {idea}The victory is described as help given to them, not something they built alone.{/idea}
now: You try to win your hard situation by yourself: more hours, more worry, more control. {idea}The victory in this verse is received, not grabbed.{/idea} {reward}Do your part, then lean on the One who helps.{/reward}
old: If I do not hold everything together myself, it will fall apart.
new: Victory for those with Allah is His help. My job is to stay with Him and do my part.
try: Before your hardest task today, ask Allah plainly for help with it.

title: Our soldiers will be the ones who overcome.
subtitle: Said when that seemed impossible
then: The surah introduction notes that {trap}no one could believe the Prophet ﷺ and his small, ill-equipped companions would ever prevail.{/trap} People thought the movement would be buried in the valleys of Makkah. {reward}Within about fifteen or sixteen years, Makkah was opened{/reward}, just as this verse had said.
now: You keep a promise nobody else keeps. You pray on time in an office that does not care. You feel tiny and outnumbered. {idea}Allah counts you among His soldiers.{/idea} Being on His side is not measured by how many stand beside you.
old: I am too small and alone for my faith to make any difference.
new: Those who belong to Allah are His soldiers, however few they look.
try: Do one act of faith today that you usually hide out of feeling outnumbered.

title: Turn away from them for a while.
subtitle: Patience with annoyance, until the appointed time
then: Ibn Kathir explains the command to the Prophet ﷺ as: {idea}bear their annoyance with patience{/idea} and wait until an appointed time, {reward}when We will grant you victory.{/reward} He was not told to answer every mockery.
now: Someone in the comments keeps mocking your faith. A relative makes the same jab at every dinner. {idea}You do not have to reply to every one.{/idea} Turning away with patience is not weakness. It is trusting that Allah has set a time.
old: If I do not answer every insult, I am letting them win.
new: Patience and turning away can be the stronger choice when the outcome is with Allah.
try: The next time someone provokes you today, do not reply. Say a quiet dua instead.

title: Watch them. They too will see.
subtitle: The waiting has an end
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}watch them and see what will happen to them{/idea} for their opposition and disbelief. Then {trap}they shall see{/trap}, which he describes as a threat and a warning. The waiting was not empty. It was leading somewhere.
now: You did the right thing and someone else got ahead by cutting corners. {trap}It looks like the corners won.{/trap} {idea}Keep watching. And keep watching yourself too{/idea}, so that when the results show, you are on the right side of them.
old: People who get away with wrong now will never face it.
new: Every outcome unfolds in Allah's time. My job is to stay on the right side of it.
try: Instead of watching someone who wronged you, check one thing in your own conduct today.

title: Are they really in a hurry for Our punishment?
subtitle: Mocking the warning by asking for it

row.title: the punishment, now
sub: bring it, if it is real

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}they sought to hasten the punishment because they disbelieved{/trap} in the Prophet ﷺ. Asking for it was their way of mocking it. {idea}Allah's question shows how foolish that is.{/idea}
now: Go on, let's see what happens, you say about a risk you know is real. Skipping the medicine. Ignoring the warning letter. {trap}Daring the consequence is not bravery.{/trap} {idea}Being given time is the mercy. Use it.{/idea}
old: If something bad were really coming, it would have come by now.
new: A warning I joke about is still a warning. The delay is mercy, not proof.
try: Stop joking about one thing you know is a real risk in your life. Take it seriously today.

title: When it arrives at their doorstep, a bad morning for the warned.
subtitle: The warning becomes real in their own homes
then: As-Suddi said the courtyard means {trap}their homes.{/trap} Ibn Kathir reports from Anas that on the morning of Khaybar, the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse. The point is in the last word: {idea}those who had been warned.{/idea} They had heard, and chose not to listen.
now: You know a habit is slowly damaging your health, your marriage, your faith. You have been warned more than once. {trap}The cost does not arrive with notice.{/trap} {idea}It is better to act while you are still being warned.{/idea}
old: I have heard all the warnings before. They are just words.
new: Being warned is a gift. The worst position is to have heard and done nothing.
try: Act today on one warning you have heard many times, about your health, family, or faith.

title: Again: turn away from them for a while.
subtitle: The command repeated, after the warning
then: Ibn Kathir notes this is {idea}a reiteration of the command stated above.{/idea} Between the two came the picture of the warned waking to a bad morning. The Prophet ﷺ is told again to be patient. {reward}The appointed time is still Allah's.{/reward}
now: You decided yesterday to stop arguing with your brother. Today he says the same thing again, and the old anger rises. {idea}You need to choose patience again.{/idea} Patience is rarely a one-time decision.
old: I already decided to be patient. If I lose it, I failed.
new: Patience is chosen again and again. Allah repeated the command, so I can repeat my choice.
try: When you lose patience today, just choose it again on the spot, without beating yourself up.

title: And see. They are going to see.
subtitle: The repeated promise that truth will show
then: Ibn Kathir notes this is {idea}a reiteration{/idea} of the earlier command. This time the verse says only see, without saying whom. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ would see the promise fulfilled{/reward}, and the deniers would see what they had mocked.
now: Years of quiet effort: the early prayers, the honest work, the kindness at home. {trap}It feels like nobody sees.{/trap} {reward}One day you will see what it built.{/reward} Keep going while you wait.
old: If I cannot see results now, there probably are none.
new: Allah promises a day of seeing. What I do in faith will show.
try: Continue one good habit today that feels like it has no visible result yet.

title: Glory to your Lord, the Lord of might.
subtitle: Free from everything they attributed to Him
then: The surah ends by returning to Allah Himself. Ibn Kathir explains Lord of Al-Izzah as {idea}the Owner of might and power Whom none can resist{/idea}, glorified far above {trap}what the lying fabricators say.{/trap} After a whole surah of false claims, this is the final word.
now: A long day of noise: opinions, arguments, headlines, your own worries. {idea}End it the way the surah ends.{/idea} Glorify your Lord, who is mightier than all of it. Let that be the last thought before sleep.
old: There is so much noise that I lose sight of who Allah is.
new: After all the noise, Allah is still glorified, mighty, and free of every false word.
try: Tonight, before sleep, recite the last three verses of this surah.

title: And peace be upon all the messengers.
subtitle: The greeting for every messenger in the surah
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as {reward}the peace of Allah upon them in this world and the Hereafter{/reward}, because what they say about their Lord is sound and true. He reports the Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}when you send salam on me, send salam on all the messengers, for I am one of the messengers.{/idea}
now: You send salawat on the Prophet ﷺ after the adhan or in the tashahhud. {idea}Remember the others too.{/idea} Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Yunus. Each one carried the same message, and each deserves your greeting.
old: Other prophets are names from long ago, not people I greet.
new: Every messenger is part of my story, and Allah greets them all with peace.
try: Today say: peace be upon all the messengers, and think of one of them by name.

title: And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: How the surah ends, and how a gathering can

row.title: praise
sub: to the Lord of the worlds

row.title: at the beginning and the end

then: Ibn Kathir explains this as {idea}praise to Him at the beginning and end of all things.{/idea} He notes that glorification and praise come together often in the Quran. He reports from Ali that whoever wants a greater reward should {reward}say these last three verses at the end of any gathering.{/reward}
now: The family dinner ends. The Zoom call wraps up. Friends stand to leave the cafe. {reward}That moment is a door.{/reward} Close it with these words. {idea}Whatever was said, the last word is praise of Allah.{/idea}
old: A gathering ends when people leave.
new: I can close any gathering with glorification, peace, and praise of Allah.
try: At the end of your next gathering today, quietly recite these last three verses.
